definition_zh: 住所；住宅；（考古）居址；居住的状态
definition_en: a place where a person or animal lives; the fact or state of living in a place
core_image: 山坡上一座低矮的石屋，屋顶压着厚草，窗内亮着一盏灯，门外只有风声
scene: 考古队在河谷台地上清理出一处下沉地面的房屋遗迹。The team uncovered a sunken-floor dwelling on the river terrace.
sceneCN: 这里 dwelling 指「供人居住的房屋」（第 1 个义项：人长期居住的建筑）；句意为考古队在河谷台地上发掘出一座地面下凹的住所。图中可辨识物件：石砌墙基、草顶残迹、门洞、散落陶片。

pos.zh: 居住用的（多用于复合词，如 dwelling house）

derivatives.zh: 居住；栖身（由「停留」义转来）
居住者；住在某处的人
住宅房屋，法律文本中与商业建筑相对
内在的；存在于内部的

senses.title: A building used as a home
senses.definition: a building or part of a building in which people live
senses.definitionCN: 供人居住的建筑物或其一部分
senses.example: The old farmhouse is the only dwelling on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老农舍是山脊上唯一的住所。
senses.why: dwelling is the noun made from the present participle of dwell, so it names the place where the staying happens.
senses.whyCN: dwelling 由「居住」这一动词的现在分词转为名词，因此指「停留这件事发生的那个地方」。

senses.title: A simple shelter rather than a house
senses.definition: a place that gives shelter, especially a simple, rough or temporary one
senses.definitionCN: 提供遮蔽的处所，尤指简陋或临时的住所
senses.example: They spent the winter in a turf dwelling cut into the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河岸上挖出的草皮小屋里过冬。
senses.why: the older verb meant simply to stay in one spot, so the noun can cover a hut or a hole as readily as a house.
senses.whyCN: 旧义只表示「待在一个地方」，所以这个词既能指房屋，也能指草棚土穴。

senses.title: A housing unit counted in official records
senses.titleCN: 统计与法规中的住宅单位
senses.definition: a unit of housing counted separately in a census or defined by housing law
senses.definitionCN: 人口普查中单独计数、或由住房法规界定的住宅单元
senses.example: The census counts each dwelling and the people inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查把每套住宅和住在里面的人分别计数。
senses.why: statistics needed a countable object, so the noun was narrowed to one self-contained place of residence.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要一个可计数的对象，这个词于是被收窄为「一套独立住宅」。

senses.title: The home of a wild animal
senses.definition: the place where a wild animal lives, such as a burrow, den or nest
senses.definitionCN: 野生动物生活的地方，如洞穴、兽窝或巢
senses.example: Badgers enlarge a dwelling that is passed down through generations.
senses.exampleCN: 獾会把一代代传下来的洞穴越挖越大。
senses.why: since dwell can be said of any creature that stays in one place, the noun followed animals as easily as people.
senses.whyCN: 既然任何长居一处的生物都能说「居住」，这个名词自然也能用于动物。

senses.title: A habitation site studied by archaeologists
senses.definition: the remains of a place where people once lived, studied as a site
senses.definitionCN: 古人曾经居住、作为遗址被研究的遗存
senses.example: The dwelling yielded pottery shards and a hearth.
senses.exampleCN: 这处居址出土了陶片和一个火塘。
senses.why: archaeology borrowed the word because it names the place of living without promising that a building still stands.
senses.whyCN: 考古学借用这个词，因为它只指明「居住过的地方」，并不保证建筑还存在。

senses.title: The state of living in a place
senses.definition: the condition or fact of living in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地点生活的状态或事实
senses.example: Forest dwelling shaped the architecture of the upland villages.
senses.exampleCN: 林中居住的生活方式塑造了高地村落的建筑。
senses.why: the participle still keeps the verb's action, so it can name the fact of living and not only the building.
senses.whyCN: 分词仍保留动词的动作义，因此既能指建筑，也能指「居住」这一事实。

senses.title: A place where a deity is said to live
senses.definition: a place where a divine being is said to live or to be present
senses.definitionCN: 据说神灵居住或降临的处所
senses.example: Pilgrims climbed toward the dwelling of the mountain god.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者向着山神的居所攀登。
senses.why: religious language reused the same image: a being that stays in one place has a dwelling there.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言沿用同一意象：长驻一处的存在，在那里就有居所。

senses.title: A house type named by its structure
senses.titleCN: 按形制划分的住屋类型
senses.definition: a category of house named by its structure or material, as a cave, stilt or cliff dwelling
senses.definitionCN: 按结构或材料命名的一类房屋，如窑洞、吊脚楼、崖居
senses.example: Stilt dwellings line the estuary to stay above the tide.
senses.exampleCN: 吊脚楼沿河口排开，以避开潮水。
senses.why: architecture turns the noun into a classifier, so one word can label many building types found around the world.
senses.whyCN: 建筑学把这个名词当作分类标签，于是一个词就能命名世界各地多种住屋形式。

intro.en: Dwelling is native English: it is the noun use of the participle of dwell, a Germanic verb recorded in Old English as dwellan. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dwelling 是英语本族词：由日耳曼语动词 dwell 的分词转作名词，该动词在古英语中写作 dwellan。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English dwellan is recorded with the sense 'to lead astray, hinder, delay', a meaning still visible in the verb's early use.
items.cn: 古英语 dwellan 有「使迷路、阻碍、延迟」的意思，这一含义在动词早期用法中仍可见到。

items.en: In Middle English the verb shifted toward 'to remain, continue in a place', and that sense drove out the older one in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 到中古英语，动词转向「停留、继续待在某地」，这一词义在日常语言中取代了旧义。

items.en: The participial noun dwelling is recorded from the late fourteenth century in the sense 'place of residence'.
items.cn: 分词名词 dwelling 自十四世纪后期起有书证，意为「居住之处」。

items.en: English law fixed the compound dwelling house, and social surveys made dwelling a countable unit of housing.
items.cn: 英国法律固定了复合词 dwelling house，社会调查又把 dwelling 变成可计数的住房单位。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no pre-Old-English form is established, and the links proposed to a Germanic root meaning 'to delay' are hypotheses rather than demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：古英语之前的形态没有定论，把它联系到某个意为「延迟」的日耳曼词根，只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to dwelling, including one different root that is often mistaken for a relative; group two holds nouns with a similar meaning but a different focus.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词，其中有一个不同词根常被误认作同族；第二组是意义相近但侧重不同的名词。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed; it means to live in a place and also, in the phrase dwell on, to keep talking or thinking about something.
entries.definitionCN: 构成该名词的动词，意为居住在某地；在 dwell on 中又指反复谈论或思考某事。

entries.definition: Dwell plus the agent suffix -er, naming the person who lives in a place, as in city dweller.
entries.definitionCN: dwell 加施事后缀 -er，指住在某处的人，如城市居民。

entries.definition: From swell 'to grow larger', not from dwell; it looks close on the page but has no family relation.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 swell「膨胀」，与 dwell 无关；书写形近，但并非同族。

entries.definition: The older irregular past and past participle of dwell, still common in British usage beside dwelled.
entries.definitionCN: dwell 较旧的规则外过去式与过去分词，在英式用法中仍常与 dwelled 并存。

entries.definition: A formal word for the home where someone lives, often used of impressive houses or official homes.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人居所的正式用词，常用于气派的宅第或官邸。

entries.definition: A literary or slightly old-fashioned word for a home, often suggesting a humble or fixed place.
entries.definitionCN: 文学性或略旧的「住所」一词，常暗示简陋或固定。

entries.definition: A formal word that stresses the act or fact of living in a place, and only secondarily the building.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用词，强调居住这一行为或事实，指建筑反而是次要的。

entries.definition: A place to stay for a time, usually paid for and not a permanent home.
entries.definitionCN: 短期居住的地方，通常付费，并非永久住所。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实复合词与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dwell plus -ing: the suffix turns the verb into the place where the staying happens.
normal.cn: dwell 加 -ing：后缀把动词变成「停留发生的那个地方」。

normal.en: The verb has two past forms, irregular dwelt and regular dwelled, and both are acceptable.
normal.cn: 这个动词有两种过去式：不规则 dwelt 与规则 dwelled，两者都可接受。

normal.en: Compounds name building types: cave dwelling, cliff dwelling, stilt dwelling.
normal.cn: 复合词标出建筑类型：窑洞、崖居、吊脚楼。

normal.en: Legal English says dwelling house when it means a building protected as a home.
normal.cn: 法律英语用 dwelling house 指受住宅法规保护的房屋。

normal.en: The family runs dwell, dweller, dwelling, indwelling.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dwell、dweller、dwelling、indwelling。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that has stayed lit in a valley for years, and the room beneath it is the dwelling.
abstract.cn: 想象山谷里一盏亮了多年的灯，灯下的那间屋子就是居所。

abstract.en: Picture a snail carrying its shell, a home that moves only because the owner moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只背着壳的蜗牛，家之所以移动，只因主人移动。

abstract.en: Picture a pin pressed into a map, and the single point under it is where life is anchored.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚按在地图上的图钉，钉尖那一点就是生活被固定下来的地方。

examples.en: The survey found that half the dwellings in the district lacked running water.
examples.cn: 调查发现该区半数住宅没有自来水。

examples.en: Owls nested in the ruined dwelling for decades.
examples.cn: 猫头鹰在那座废弃的住所里筑巢数十年。

examples.en: The law protects a dwelling from being demolished without a permit.
examples.cn: 法律保护住宅，未经许可不得拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dwell（停留）+ ing」——停下来不走的地方 → 住所、居所

root: 古英语 dwellan「使迷路、延迟」→ 中古英语「停留、居留」；分词 dwelling 转指「住所」。古英语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a creature stays in one place, and the place of that staying becomes a home, a counted housing unit, an animal burrow, an excavated site and finally a building type.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：生物在一处停留，停留之处便成为家、可计数的住宅、动物洞穴、考古居址，最后成为一类建筑形制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room that stays put while everything outside moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮着灯的屋子停在原处，屋外一切都在移动。

branches.en: STAYING AND ITS FACT: the act of staying and the place of staying are two sides of the same participle.
branches.cn: 停留与停留之事：停留的动作与停留的地点，是同一个分词的两面。

branches.en: ANIMAL HOME: any creature that stays put has a dwelling, so the word crosses the line between people and beasts.
branches.cn: 动物的家：任何长居一处的生物都有居所，这个词因此跨越人与兽的界限。

branches.en: COUNTED AND EXCAVATED: officials count a dwelling as a unit, while archaeologists read it as a site of remains.
branches.cn: 计数与发掘：官员把住宅当作统计单位，考古学家则把它读作遗存遗址。

branches.en: SHELTER AND SACRED PLACE: both keep the simple image of a place where someone or something stays.
branches.cn: 栖身与神圣处所：两者都保留「某人或某物停留之处」这一朴素意象。

branches.en: BUILDING TYPE: architecture turns the noun into a label for cave, cliff and stilt homes.
branches.cn: 建筑类型：建筑学把这个名词变成窑洞、崖居与吊脚楼的标签。

intro.en: Dwelling is a native English formation, a Germanic verb plus an English suffix, so it reads quite differently from the Latin-built words around it.
intro.cn: dwelling 是英语本族构词：日耳曼语动词加英语后缀，因此与周围那些拉丁构词读法很不一样。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin forms are listed; its formal neighbours such as habitation come from a separate Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，故不列拉丁词形；habitation 等正式近邻来自另一个拉丁词族。

items.meaning: to live in a place; to remain
items.example: They dwell above the timber line.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在林线以上。

items.meaning: the act, result or place of doing something
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for the place.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成地点的名称。

items.example: A single dwelling stood by the ford.
items.exampleCN: 渡口边只有一座住所。

items.meaning: a person who lives in a place
items.example: The cliff dwellers kept goats in the gorge.
items.exampleCN: 崖居者在峡谷里养山羊。

items.meaning: a person or thing that performs the action
items.example: The suffix marks the one who acts.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出动作的执行者。

items.meaning: a house protected as a residence
items.meaningCN: 受住宅法规保护的房屋
items.example: The statute defines a dwelling house as a self-contained home.
items.exampleCN: 该法规把住宅房屋界定为独立成套的住所。

items.meaning: one self-contained home in a building
items.meaningCN: 一栋建筑中独立成套的一套住宅
items.example: Each dwelling unit has its own entrance.
items.exampleCN: 每套住宅都有自己的入口。

items.example: Theology speaks of an indwelling presence.
items.exampleCN: 神学谈论一种内住的存在。

items.meaning: the length of time spent in one place or state
items.example: Engineers measure the dwell time of each batch.
items.exampleCN: 工程师测量每一批料的停留时间。

definition_zh: 居住；住所；人类定居的痕迹；居住权
definition_en: the act of living in a place; a place where people live; the fact of an area having been lived in
core_image: 河湾边几间石屋围着一口水井，炊烟连成一条线，远处是无人走动的荒坡
scene: 测绘员在荒原边缘发现了几处废弃的石屋。The surveyors found traces of former habitation at the edge of the moor.
sceneCN: 这里 habitation 指「人类居住留下的痕迹」（第 3 个义项：某地曾有人居住的证据）；句意为测绘员在荒原边缘发现了旧日居住的痕迹。图中可辨识物件：石墙残基、井口、塌落的屋顶、草甸。

pos.zh: 居住；住所；（某地的）居住痕迹
居住权（大陆法系中的一种物权）

derivatives.zh: 居住于；栖居于（前缀 in- 表示「在内」）
居民；住户；栖居动物
可居住的（-able 表示「能够」）
无人居住的（un- 加 -ed 构成否定形容词）

senses.title: The act of living in a place
senses.definition: the act or fact of living in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地点生活这一行为或事实
senses.example: Signs of habitation appeared only after the river changed course.
senses.exampleCN: 直到河流改道之后，才出现居住的迹象。
senses.why: habitation is the Latin noun of action from habitare 'to dwell', so its first job is to name the act, not the building.
senses.whyCN: habitation 是拉丁动词 habitare「居住」的行为名词，因此它首先指动作，而不是建筑。

senses.title: A place where someone lives
senses.definition: a place in which someone lives, especially a simple or isolated one
senses.definitionCN: 某人生活的地方，尤指简陋或偏僻的住所
senses.example: The trapper built a habitation of logs and turf beside the creek.
senses.exampleCN: 捕兽人在溪边用原木和草皮搭了一处住所。
senses.why: Latin already used the same noun for the result as well as the act, so English inherited both readings at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本就用同一个名词兼指动作与结果，英语因此同时继承了两层意思。

senses.title: Evidence that people lived in an area
senses.definition: the fact or signs of people having lived in an area, as shown by remains
senses.definitionCN: 某地曾有人居住的事实或迹象，以遗存为证
senses.example: Charred stones marked the first habitation on the plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 烧黑的石块标出了高原上最早的居住痕迹。
senses.why: field surveys needed a word for occupancy itself, so habitation came to mean the trace of living rather than the dwelling.
senses.whyCN: 野外调查需要一个指「占用」本身的词，habitation 于是指居住的痕迹，而非房屋。

senses.title: The condition of being fit to live in
senses.definition: the condition of being safe and suitable for people to live in
senses.definitionCN: 安全且适合人居住的状态
senses.example: Inspectors judged the block unfit for habitation.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员判定这栋楼不宜居住。
senses.why: housing law asks whether a place can be lived in at all, and the noun supplied that abstract condition.
senses.whyCN: 住房法规要判断一个地方究竟能否住人，这个名词正好提供了这一抽象状态。

senses.title: A dwelling counted as a housing unit
senses.titleCN: 作为住房单位计数的住所
senses.definition: a house or flat treated as one unit of housing in records
senses.definitionCN: 在登记中被视为一个住房单位的房屋或公寓
senses.example: The new rule applies to every habitation with its own kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定适用于每一套带独立厨房的住所。
senses.why: administration prefers a countable noun, and habitation was narrowed to one self-contained place of living.
senses.whyCN: 行政文书偏爱可数名词，habitation 因此被收窄为「一套独立住所」。

senses.title: A legal right to live in another's house
senses.definition: a limited right in civil law to live in a house owned by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 大陆法系中在他人家中居住的有限权利
senses.example: Her will granted him a habitation for the rest of his life.
senses.exampleCN: 她的遗嘱授予他终身居住权。
senses.why: Roman law separated the right to use a house from ownership, and the old noun was kept for that right.
senses.whyCN: 罗马法把房屋的使用权与所有权分开，这个古老名词就被保留下来指该项权利。

senses.title: A small settlement or group of homes
senses.definition: a group of homes forming a small settlement, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 由若干住宅构成的小型聚落，常用复数
senses.example: Scattered habitations dot the valley floor.
senses.exampleCN: 零散的居民点散布在谷底。
senses.why: plural use turns the word into a map label for a cluster of homes rather than one building.
senses.whyCN: 复数用法把这个词变成地图上标注一片住宅的标签，而非单座建筑。

senses.title: A place associated with a divine presence
senses.definition: a place associated with a god or an unseen being said to be present there
senses.definitionCN: 与神灵或无形存在有关的处所
senses.example: The grove was treated as the habitation of the forest spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 那片树林被视为林灵的居所。
senses.why: religious language extended the ordinary noun for living somewhere to beings that are not seen.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言把日常表示「住在某处」的名词，扩展到看不见的存在身上。

intro.en: Habitation comes from Latin habitatio 'a dwelling', from habitare 'to dwell', which is a frequentative form of habere 'to have, hold'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: habitation 来自拉丁 habitatio「住所」，源自 habitare「居住」，而 habitare 是 habere「持有」的反复动词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Habere meant 'to have, hold, keep'. The often-cited Indo-European base is a reconstruction, and how 'hold' turned into 'dwell' is debated.
items.cn: habere 意为「拥有、持有、守住」。常被引用的印欧语词基属于重构形式，而「持有」如何转为「居住」仍有争论。

items.en: Habitare, a frequentative of habere, meant 'to dwell, to keep on occupying a place', literally 'to be holding' it.
items.cn: habitare 是 habere 的反复形式，意为「居住、持续占有一地」，字面就是「一直持有着」。

items.en: The action noun habitatio named both the act of dwelling and the place where one dwells.
items.cn: 行为名词 habitatio 同时指「居住」这一动作和「居住的地方」。

items.en: Old French habitation brought the word into English in the thirteenth century, first as the act and soon after as the place.
items.cn: 古法语 habitation 在十三世纪把该词带入英语，先指动作，很快也指地点。

items.en: Civil-law texts kept a specialised sense, the right of habitation, meaning a limited personal right to live in another's house.
items.cn: 大陆法文本保留了一个专门义「居住权」，指在他人家中居住的有限人身权利。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not fixed to a single year, and the pre-Latin base of habere is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证无法系于某一年，habere 的拉丁语前词基属于重构形式而非有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical forms that come from the same Latin verb but mean different things; group two holds nouns that also speak of living somewhere.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词，同出拉丁动词却意义不同；第二组是同样表示「住在某处」的名词。

entries.definition: The natural environment in which a species lives, not the building or settlement; it is the sense ecology fixed for the word.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种生活的自然环境，而非建筑或聚落；这是生态学为它固定的含义。

entries.definition: From Latin habitus 'condition, bearing', it means a repeated behaviour or a garment worn by monks, not a place of living.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 habitus「状态、举止」，指重复的习惯或僧侣的袍服，并非居住之处。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus habitare: the verb meaning to live in a place, from which inhabitant is formed.
entries.definitionCN: in-「在内」加 habitare：表示居住在某地的动词，inhabitant 由它构成。

entries.definition: Built on habit in its behaviour sense, meaning done regularly; it belongs to the habit branch, not the dwelling branch.
entries.definitionCN: 由「习惯」义的 habit 构成，意为惯常的；属于「习惯」分支，而非「居住」分支。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for the house or shelter where someone lives; habitation is more formal and can mean the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指人所住房屋或遮蔽处的日常名词；habitation 更正式，且可指居住行为。

entries.definition: A formal word for a home, often an imposing house or an official one; it stresses status more than shelter.
entries.definitionCN: 指住所的正式用词，常指气派的宅第或官邸，更强调身份而非遮蔽。

entries.definition: The fact of using or living in a space, often temporary or legally measured; it does not imply a permanent home.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用或占用一处空间的事实，常为临时或按法规计量；并不暗示永久安家。

entries.definition: A place where people have settled as a community, larger than a single dwelling and mapped as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 人们作为群体定居的地方，规模大于单座住所，在地图上成片标出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real legal phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实法律短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: habere 'hold' plus the frequentative -itare: to keep holding a place, hence to dwell there.
normal.cn: habere「持有」加反复后缀 -itare：一直持有一地，因此就是住在那里。

normal.en: The same root gives inhabit, inhabitant, habitable and uninhabited.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 inhabit、inhabitant、habitable 与 uninhabited。

normal.en: Legal phrases keep the old noun alive: right of habitation, fit for habitation.
normal.cn: 法律短语让这个古老名词延续：居住权、适宜居住。

normal.en: Keep habitat apart: habitat is the environment, habitation is the living there.
normal.cn: 要把 habitat 分清：habitat 是环境，habitation 是居住这件事。

normal.en: Surveys say signs of habitation when they mean traces of people, not houses still standing.
normal.cn: 调查报告说「居住痕迹」时，指的是人留下的痕迹，而非仍然立着的房屋。

abstract.en: Picture a footprint that outlasts the foot, which is exactly what a trace of habitation is.
abstract.cn: 想象一个比脚留得更久的脚印，居住痕迹正是如此。

abstract.en: Picture a key that grants the right to sleep under a roof without owning it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，给人睡在屋顶下的权利，却不给所有权。

abstract.en: Picture a map with three dots that mean homes rather than points.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上三个圆点，它们代表的是家，而不是坐标。

examples.en: The valley has shown continuous habitation for more than four thousand years.
examples.cn: 这个山谷显示出四千多年连续不断的居住史。

examples.en: The council declared the building unfit for habitation after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，市政会宣布该建筑不宜居住。

examples.en: A few habitations cling to the slope above the road.
examples.cn: 几处住所紧贴在大路以上的山坡上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「habit（习惯）+ ation」——习惯待在一个地方 → 居住、住所

root: 拉丁 habere「持有」→ 反复动词 habitare「一直占有一地、居住」→ 名词 habitatio「居住；住所」。habere 的拉丁语前词基为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one Latin act noun: holding a place becomes living there, then the place itself, the trace left behind, the legal right to stay, and even a god's home.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由一个拉丁行为名词展开：持有一地成为居住，继而指处所本身、留下的痕迹、居住的权利，甚至神灵的居所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that keeps hold of one spot of ground until staying there becomes living there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手始终抓住一小块地面，抓久了，停留就成了居住。

branches.en: ACT AND PLACE: the same Latin noun named both the living there and the place where it happens.
branches.cn: 动作与地点：同一个拉丁名词既指居住，也指居住之处。

branches.en: TRACE: surveyors read the remains of living as evidence that the place was once inhabited.
branches.cn: 痕迹：调查者把生活遗存读作「这里曾有人住」的证据。

branches.en: MEASURED LIVING: law asks whether a place is fit to live in and counts it as one housing unit.
branches.cn: 可量度的居住：法律判断一处能否住人，并把它计作一个住房单位。

branches.en: RIGHT: Roman law split use from ownership, leaving a limited personal right to live in another's house.
branches.cn: 权利：罗马法把使用与所有权分开，留下在他人家中居住的有限人身权利。

branches.en: MAP AND MYTH: the plural labels a cluster of homes, and religious language lends the noun to unseen beings.
branches.cn: 地图与神话：复数形式标注一片住宅，宗教语言则把这个名词借给看不见的存在。

intro.en: Habitation is built entirely from Latin material: a root meaning 'hold', a frequentative suffix and a noun suffix, all still productive in English.
intro.cn: habitation 完全由拉丁材料构成：意为「持有」的词根、反复后缀与名词后缀，这些成分在英语中仍有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere gives habitation, inhabit, inhabitant, habitable, habit and habitat; in- adds 'within', while -atio forms the action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 habere 衍生 habitation、inhabit、inhabitant、habitable、habit 与 habitat；in- 增添「在内」，-atio 构成行为名词。

items.example: The root carries the idea of holding on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「抓住不放」的意思。

items.meaning: to do something repeatedly or intensively
items.example: The suffix makes holding into continuing to hold.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「持有」变成「持续持有」。

items.meaning: to dwell, to keep occupying a place
items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成动作的名称。

items.meaning: living in a place; a place lived in
items.example: The word covers both the act and the place.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼指动作与地点。

items.example: Few animals inhabit the salt flat.
items.exampleCN: 很少有动物栖居在这片盐滩。

items.meaning: one who lives in a place
items.example: The island has fewer than a hundred inhabitants.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛的居民不到一百人。

items.example: Only the lower slopes are habitable.
items.exampleCN: 只有较低的山坡可以住人。

items.meaning: the environment where a species lives
items.example: Drainage destroyed the bird's habitat.
items.exampleCN: 排水工程毁掉了这种鸟的栖息地。

latinEntries.meaning: a dwelling; the act of dwelling

definition_zh: 居民；住户；（某环境的）栖居动物
definition_en: a person or animal that lives in a particular place
core_image: 清晨的巷口，一个提着水罐的人从门里走出，脚下的石板被无数双脚磨得发亮
scene: 岛上的每一户人家都在请愿书上签了名。Every inhabitant of the island signed the petition.
sceneCN: 这里 inhabitant 指「长期住在某地的人」（第 1 个义项：某地的常住居民）；句意为岛上的每一位居民都在请愿书上签了名。图中可辨识物件：门廊、水罐、签名纸、海堤。

derivatives.zh: 居住于；栖居于
有人居住的（-ed 构成形容词）
可居住的（-able 表示「能够」）
无人居住的（un- 表否定）

senses.title: A person who lives in a place
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular place, especially one who lives there permanently
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地点生活的人，尤指长期居住者
senses.example: Every inhabitant of the valley knew the old path.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里的每一位居民都认得那条旧路。
senses.why: inhabitant is the present participle of inhabit used as a noun, so it names the one who is doing the living.
senses.whyCN: inhabitant 是「居住」这一动词的现在分词转名词，因此指「正在居住的那个人」。

senses.title: A resident counted by officials
senses.definition: a person recorded as living in a house, district or country for official purposes
senses.definitionCN: 因行政用途被登记为住在某屋、某区或某国的人
senses.example: The census lists two thousand inhabitants in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查登记该镇有两千名居民。
senses.why: governments need a countable person attached to a place, and this noun supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要一个与地点绑定、可计数的人，这个名词正好提供这一角色。

senses.title: One of the earliest people of a region
senses.definition: a person belonging to the earliest people known to have lived in a region
senses.definitionCN: 属于某地已知最早居住人群的人
senses.example: The museum recorded the songs of the first inhabitants.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆记录了最早居民的歌谣。
senses.why: history needed to distinguish those who were there first from later arrivals, and the plain noun took on that contrast.
senses.whyCN: 历史叙述需要区分「先在那里的人」与后来者，这个普通名词便承担了这一对比。

senses.title: An animal or plant living in a habitat
senses.definition: an animal or plant that lives in a particular environment
senses.definitionCN: 生活在特定环境中的动物或植物
senses.example: Beetles are the most numerous inhabitants of the forest floor.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫是林地地表数量最多的栖居者。
senses.why: since inhabit can take an animal as its subject, the noun extends to any creature that lives in a place.
senses.whyCN: 既然这一动词的主语可以是动物，这个名词就扩展到任何栖居一地的生物。

senses.title: A person who occupies a house
senses.definition: someone who occupies a building, whether as owner or tenant
senses.definitionCN: 占用某栋建筑的人，无论业主还是租客
senses.example: The landlord must warn every inhabitant before repairs begin.
senses.exampleCN: 房东在动工维修前必须通知每一位住户。
senses.why: housing law speaks of inhabitants rather than owners because it cares about who is inside the building.
senses.whyCN: 住房法规说的是「住户」而非业主，因为它关心的是谁住在楼里。

senses.title: A being imagined on another world
senses.definition: a being supposed to live on another planet or moon
senses.definitionCN: 被设想生活在其他行星或卫星上的存在
senses.example: Writers once peopled Mars with gentle inhabitants.
senses.exampleCN: 作家们曾给火星安上温和的居民。
senses.why: the noun needed no new form for imagined worlds, because it only says that someone lives somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不需要为想象世界另造新形，因为它只表示「有谁住在某处」。

senses.title: A member of a community defined by place
senses.titleCN: 按地域界定的人群成员
senses.definition: a member of a community identified by where they live rather than by kinship
senses.definitionCN: 按居住地而非血缘识别的人群成员
senses.example: City inhabitants and villagers use the river differently.
senses.exampleCN: 城市居民与村民使用这条河的方式不同。
senses.why: social writing uses the noun to group people by settlement, turning geography into a category.
senses.whyCN: 社会写作借这个词按聚落给人分类，把地理变成类别。

senses.title: A figurative resident of an era or medium
senses.titleCN: 抽象世界中的居民（比喻义）
senses.definition: a person or thing that seems to belong naturally to a particular era, medium or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 似乎天然属于某个时代、媒介或生活方式的人或物
senses.example: She is an inhabitant of the age of print, not of the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 她属于印刷时代，而不属于屏幕时代。
senses.why: the abstract sense treats an era or medium as a territory that one can live inside.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把时代或媒介当作一块可以住在里面的疆域。

intro.en: Inhabitant comes from Latin inhabitans, the present participle of inhabitare 'to dwell in', built on in- 'in' and habitare 'to dwell'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inhabitant 来自拉丁 inhabitans，即 inhabitare「住在里面」的现在分词，由 in-「在内」与 habitare「居住」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Habitare 'to dwell' is a frequentative of habere 'to hold', so dwelling is pictured as continuing to hold a place.
items.cn: habitare「居住」是 habere「持有」的反复形式，因此「居住」被设想为持续占有一地。

items.en: The prefix in- 'in, within' made inhabitare, 'to live in a place', with the participle inhabitans 'the one living in'.
items.cn: 前缀 in-「在内」构成 inhabitare「住在某地」，其分词 inhabitans 意为「住在里面的人」。

items.en: Old French inhabitant passed the participle into English, where it was treated as a noun rather than a verb form.
items.cn: 古法语 inhabitant 把这个分词传入英语，英语把它当作名词而非动词形式使用。

items.en: For centuries the word was used mainly of people; later natural history extended it to animals and plants of a region.
items.cn: 数百年间该词主要用于人；后来博物学把它扩展到一地的动物与植物。

items.en: Official counting and housing law fixed phrases such as every inhabitant, giving the noun a precise administrative role.
items.cn: 官方统计与住房法规固定了 every inhabitant 一类说法，使该名词具备精确的行政用途。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact year of the earliest English use is not settled, and the pre-Latin base of habere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语用例确切年份尚无定论，habere 的拉丁语前词基仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin stock whose meanings have split; group two holds words for people living in a place, each with a different legal or social slant.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词源但词义已分化的词；第二组是表示「住在某地的人」的词，法律或社会侧重各不相同。

entries.definition: The verb 'to live in a place'; the noun inhabitant is its participle turned into a person word.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「居住于」的动词；名词 inhabitant 是它的分词转成指人的词。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a place where people live, as opposed to uninhabited.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某地有人居住的形容词，与无人居住相对。

entries.definition: A noun for the act of living somewhere or the place itself; it does not name the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指居住行为或居住地点的名词，并不指人。

entries.definition: The natural environment of a species; it is the place, never the creature that lives in it.
entries.definitionCN: 物种的自然环境；指地点，绝不指住在其中的生物。

entries.definition: A person officially living at an address; it stresses registration and duration more than inhabitant does.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地址正式居住的人；比 inhabitant 更强调登记与居住时长。

entries.definition: A plainer word for someone who lives in a place, usually in compounds such as city dweller.
entries.definitionCN: 指住在某地者的朴素说法，多用于 city dweller 一类复合词。

entries.definition: A person who is in and using a space at a given time, whether or not it is their home.
entries.definitionCN: 指某时正占用一处空间的人，不论那里是否为其家。

entries.definition: A person born in a place, which adds birth to the plain idea of living there.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地出生的人，在「住在那里」之外又加上「生于那里」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real administrative phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实行政短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'in' + habitare 'dwell' + -ant 'one who': the one dwelling inside.
normal.cn: in-「在内」+ habitare「居住」+ -ant「做某事的人」：住在里面的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs inhabit, inhabitant, inhabited, uninhabited, inhabitable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 inhabit、inhabitant、inhabited、uninhabited、inhabitable。

normal.en: Census language makes it countable: a town of five thousand inhabitants.
normal.cn: 人口普查语言让它可数：五千居民的小镇。

normal.en: Natural-history writing uses it for animals: the inhabitants of a tide pool.
normal.cn: 博物写作把它用于动物：潮池里的栖居者。

normal.en: Keep habitat separate: habitat is where a species lives, inhabitant is the species living there.
normal.cn: 要把 habitat 分清：habitat 是物种生活的环境，inhabitant 是住在其中的生物。

abstract.en: Picture a nameplate on a door that lists not the owner but the person who sleeps there.
abstract.cn: 想象门上的名牌写的不是房主，而是睡在里面的人。

abstract.en: Picture a dot on a census map that stands for a whole life, not a coordinate.
abstract.cn: 想象人口普查图上的一个点，它代表一整段生活，而不是一个坐标。

abstract.en: Picture a person who fits an old library so well that the era seems to be their address.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人与旧图书馆如此契合，仿佛那个时代就是他的住址。

examples.en: The village has only sixty inhabitants, most of them over seventy.
examples.cn: 这个村子只有六十名居民，多数已过七十岁。

examples.en: The first inhabitants arrived by boat about nine thousand years ago.
examples.cn: 最早的居民大约九千年前乘船到达。

examples.en: Frogs are the loudest inhabitants of the marsh at night.
examples.cn: 青蛙是夜里沼泽中最喧闹的栖居者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（里面）+ habit（习惯）+ ant（人）」——习惯住在里面的人 → 居民

root: 拉丁 in-「在内」+ habitare「居住」（habere「持有」的反复形式）+ -ant「做某事的人」；英语经古法语 inhabitant 借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person: the one who lives there, the one counted, the one there first, the animal in a habitat, the tenant inside a building, the imagined Martian, the member of a place-based group, and finally anyone who seems to belong to an era.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个人展开：住在那里的人、被统计的人、最早在那里的人、栖息一地的动物、楼里的住户、想象中的火星居民、按地域归类的人群成员，最后是仿佛属于某个时代的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing inside a marked boundary, whose presence makes the place inhabited.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在划定的边界之内，他的存在使这个地方成为有人居住之地。

branches.en: PERSON AND NUMBER: the same noun names one resident and supplies the unit for counting a whole population.
branches.cn: 人与数：同一个名词既指一位居民，也提供统计全体人口的计数单位。

branches.en: FIRSTNESS: history adds the question of who was there earliest, turning residence into origin.
branches.cn: 先在：历史叙述加上「谁最早在那里」的问题，把居住变成出身。

branches.en: OTHER SPECIES: ecology applies the person word to animals and plants of a habitat.
branches.cn: 其他物种：生态学把这个指人的词用于栖息地中的动植物。

branches.en: INSIDE AND GROUPED: law cares who occupies the building, while social writing groups people by settlement.
branches.cn: 在内与归类：法律关心谁占用这栋楼，社会写作则按聚落给人分类。

branches.en: IMAGINED TERRITORY: planets and eras become territories that can have residents.
branches.cn: 想象疆域：行星与时代都成为可以有居民的疆域。

intro.en: Inhabitant is a Latin participle used as an English noun: a prefix, a frequentative root and a participial suffix, each still recognisable in other words.
intro.cn: inhabitant 是当作英语名词使用的拉丁分词：前缀、反复词根与分词后缀，三者在其他词中仍可辨认。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere 'hold' gives habitare 'dwell' and then inhabitare 'dwell in'; in- marks position inside, and -ant marks the person doing it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 habere「持有」派生 habitare「居住」，再派生 inhabitare「住在里面」；in- 标出内部位置，-ant 标出执行动作的人。

items.example: The prefix places the action inside a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放进某个边界之内。

items.example: The verb describes living as continued holding.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把居住描述为持续的持有。

items.example: Only a few families inhabit the upper valley.
items.exampleCN: 只有几户人家住在上游谷地。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into the person performing it.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成执行动作的人。

items.meaning: one who lives in a place
items.example: Each inhabitant received a copy of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 每位居民都收到了一份规划。

items.example: The islands are thinly inhabited.
items.exampleCN: 这些岛屿人烟稀少。

items.example: The cave is barely inhabitable in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这个洞穴冬天几乎无法住人。

items.example: An uninhabited island lies beyond the reef.
items.exampleCN: 礁石之外有一座无人岛。

items.meaning: the act of living in a place
items.example: The site shows centuries of inhabitation.
items.exampleCN: 该遗址显示出数百年的居住史。

latinEntries.meaning: dwelling in; one who dwells in

definition_en: a job or profession; the act of taking and holding a place; the use of a space or time
core_image: 一间窄小的办公室，桌上摊着考勤表，墙上挂着工厂排班图，窗外是施工围栏
scene: 历史学家在旧档案里读到，这座城曾被外来军队控制多年。The archive shows that the city lived through a long occupation.
sceneCN: 这里 occupation 指「军事占领」（第 2 个义项：以武力控制并驻守某地）；句意为档案显示这座城市经历了一段漫长的占领时期。图中可辨识物件：军旗、检查站、旧地图、档案盒。

senses.title: A job or profession
senses.definition: the work a person does regularly to earn a living
senses.definitionCN: 一个人为谋生而长期从事的工作
senses.example: Her occupation is listed as laboratory technician.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职业登记为实验室技术员。
senses.why: a job takes up a person's time and attention, so the Latin verb for seizing a place was applied to seizing a day.
senses.whyCN: 工作会占去人的时间与精力，于是拉丁语中「占据地方」的动词被用来指「占去一天」。

senses.title: Military seizure and control of a place
senses.definition: the act of taking control of a country or region by armed force and staying there
senses.definitionCN: 以武力夺取并驻守控制某国或某地区的行为
senses.example: The museum closed during the occupation and lost part of its collection.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在占领期间关闭，部分藏品散失。
senses.why: the core meaning is seizing and holding, which is exactly what an army does to a territory.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是「夺取并占住」，这正是一支军队对一片土地所做的事。

senses.title: The act of filling or using a space
senses.definition: the act of taking up and using a building, room or piece of land
senses.definitionCN: 占用并使用某栋建筑、房间或一块土地的行为
senses.example: Occupation of the new wing begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 新侧楼的启用入住从九月开始。
senses.why: from holding a territory to holding a room is a short step: in both cases something is taken and kept.
senses.whyCN: 从占住一片土地到占住一个房间只差一步：两件事都是「拿下来并保持住」。

senses.title: The state of being busy
senses.definition: the condition of being busy or having one's attention fully taken up
senses.definitionCN: 忙于某事、注意力被完全占去的状态
senses.example: He found occupation for his hands in repairing the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠修篱笆让双手有事可做。
senses.why: the same verb can mean to keep someone busy, and the noun records that state of being taken up.
senses.whyCN: 同一动词也可表示「使人忙于某事」，名词便记录这种被占满的状态。

senses.title: Lawful possession of property
senses.definition: the legal holding or tenancy of land or buildings
senses.definitionCN: 对土地或建筑的合法持有或租用
senses.example: The tenant's occupation of the flat is protected by statute.
senses.exampleCN: 租客对该公寓的占有受法规保护。
senses.why: property law uses the word for the fact of holding premises, whether by owner or tenant.
senses.whyCN: 财产法用这个词指持有房屋这一事实，无论持有者是业主还是租客。

senses.title: A pastime that fills the time
senses.definition: an activity pursued for interest rather than for pay
senses.definitionCN: 出于兴趣而非报酬从事的活动
senses.example: Gardening is his favourite occupation on free afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是他空闲下午最喜爱的消遣。
senses.why: because occupation means whatever takes up one's time, it covers unpaid hobbies as well as paid work.
senses.whyCN: 既然 occupation 指「占去时间的事」，它自然既包括有薪工作，也包括无偿爱好。

senses.title: Settlement of land by newcomers
senses.titleCN: 外来者对土地的定居占用
senses.definition: the settling and use of land by people who move onto it, often without formal title
senses.definitionCN: 迁入者定居并使用土地，常无正式产权
senses.example: Early occupation of the riverbank was informal and unrecorded.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸早期的占用是非正式的，也没有记录。
senses.why: history uses the word for land taken and held by settlers, keeping the original idea of seizure.
senses.whyCN: 历史叙述用这个词指移居者取得并占住的土地，保留了「夺取」的原义。

senses.title: Something that fills the mind
senses.definition: a thought, worry or interest that takes up one's mind
senses.definitionCN: 占去心思的想法、忧虑或兴趣
senses.example: The unfinished novel became his constant occupation.
senses.exampleCN: 那部未完成的小说成了他时刻挂心的事。
senses.why: the abstract sense treats the mind as a space that can be taken and held like a city.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把心灵当作一块可以像城池一样被占据、被守住的空地。

intro.en: Occupation comes from Latin occupatio, from occupare 'to seize, take possession of', built on ob- 'against, over' and capere 'to take, grasp'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: occupation 来自拉丁 occupatio，源自动词 occupare「夺取、占有」，由 ob-「对着、在上」与 capere「拿、抓」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Capere meant 'to take, seize, grasp'. The Indo-European base often cited for it is a reconstruction, and related forms appear across the Italic languages.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、夺取、抓」。常为其引用的印欧语词基属于重构形式，相关形态在意大利语族各语言中均有出现。

items.en: Ob- 'against, over' plus capere produced occupare 'to seize, take possession of, keep busy'.
items.cn: ob-「对着、在上」加 capere 构成 occupare「夺取、占有、使忙碌」。

items.en: The noun occupatio named the act of seizing and, by extension, whatever takes up one's time or attention.
items.cn: 名词 occupatio 指夺取行为，并引申指占去时间或注意力的事物。

items.en: Old French occupacion brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of holding a place or a post.
items.cn: 古法语 occupacion 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，最初指占住一个地方或职位。

items.en: War reporting fixed the military sense, while property law kept the older sense of lawful holding of premises.
items.cn: 战地报道固定了军事义，财产法则保留了「合法持有房屋」的旧义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of capere is reconstructed, and the exact force of ob- in this compound is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：capere 的拉丁语前形态属于重构形式，ob- 在该复合词中的确切作用仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same Latin verb where the ending decides the meaning; group two holds words for the work someone does.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词、靠词尾区分意义的词形；第二组是表示「所从事的工作」的词。

entries.definition: To take and hold a place, fill a space or keep someone busy; the noun occupation is its action form.
entries.definitionCN: 指占据并保有某地、占满空间或使人忙碌；名词 occupation 是它的行为形式。

entries.definition: The person who is in and using a place at a given time, not the job that person does.
entries.definitionCN: 指某时正在使用某处的人，而不是此人所做的职业。

entries.definition: The state or rate of a place being used, as in hotel occupancy; it measures filling, not employment.
entries.definitionCN: 指某处被使用的状态或比率，如酒店入住率；衡量的是占用，不是就业。

entries.definition: Pre- 'beforehand' plus occupied: whose attention was taken up in advance, hence absent-minded.
entries.definitionCN: pre-「事先」加 occupied：注意力事先已被占去，因此显得心不在焉。

entries.definition: A job requiring specialised training and often a formal qualification, such as law or medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 需要专门训练、通常有正式资格的职位，如法律或医学。

entries.definition: The whole course of a person's working life, viewed as a progression rather than one job.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人整个工作历程，被看作递进过程而非单一职位。

entries.definition: The state of having paid work, or the work itself; it stresses the employer relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有有薪工作的状态或该工作本身，强调雇佣关系。

entries.definition: A skilled craft or manual occupation, such as carpentry, often learned through apprenticeship.
entries.definitionCN: 指需要手艺的行业或体力职业，如木工，常通过学徒制习得。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real legal and military phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实法律与军事短语、真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ob- 'over' + capere 'seize': to seize and hold, whether a city, a room or a whole day.
normal.cn: ob-「在上」+ capere「抓取」：抓住并占住，无论是一座城、一间屋还是一整天。

normal.en: The family runs occupy, occupant, occupancy, occupation, occupational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 occupy、occupant、occupancy、occupation、occupational。

normal.en: The job sense survives in forms asking for your occupation at the bank or the clinic.
normal.cn: 职业义仍活在银行或诊所让你填写职业的表格里。

normal.en: Military phrases keep the original force: occupation forces, under occupation.
normal.cn: 军事短语保留了原义的力量：占领军、处于占领之下。

normal.en: Property law says occupation of the premises for the fact of holding a building.
normal.cn: 财产法用 occupation of the premises 指持有房屋这一事实。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled up to a desk and never moved, holding the same person for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一把拉到桌前的椅子多年不动，一直占着同一个人。

abstract.en: Picture a flag planted on a hill, and the ground beneath it is no longer freely entered.
abstract.cn: 想象一面插在山头的旗，旗下的土地从此不再可自由进入。

abstract.en: Picture a single idea sitting in a room of the mind and refusing to leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头坐在心灵的某个房间里，不肯离开。

examples.en: Please state your name, age and occupation on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上填写姓名、年龄和职业。

examples.en: The occupation lasted seven years and ended with a treaty.
examples.cn: 占领持续了七年，以一项条约结束。

examples.en: Reading was her only occupation during the long recovery.
examples.cn: 在漫长的康复期间，阅读是她唯一的消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oc（一再）+ cup（杯子）+ ation」——一只杯子被反复占住 → 占据、职业

root: 拉丁 ob-「对着、在上」+ capere「抓取」→ occupare「夺取、占有」→ occupatio「占据；职业」。capere 的拉丁语前形态为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of seizing and holding: an army holds a country, a tenant holds a flat, a job holds a day, a hobby holds an afternoon, and finally a thought holds the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「夺取并占住」这一动作展开：军队占住国家，租客占住公寓，职业占去一天，爱好占去一个下午，最后是一个念头占住心灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing over a place and not letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢在一处地方上，不再松开。

branches.en: TAKING AND HOLDING LAND: armies and settlers both seize ground and stay on it.
branches.cn: 夺取并占住土地：军队与移居者都夺取地面并留在上面。

branches.en: HOLDING PREMISES: a room or a building can be occupied, lawfully or merely in fact.
branches.cn: 持有房屋：房间或建筑可以被占用，或合法，或仅成事实。

branches.en: WORK AS TAKING TIME: a job is what regularly takes up the greater part of the day.
branches.cn: 工作即占去时间：职业就是经常占去一天中大部分时间的事。

branches.en: FILLING TIME: being busy and pursuing a pastime are the same filling seen with and without pay.
branches.cn: 填满时间：忙碌与消遣是同一个「填满」，只是一个有报酬、一个没有。

branches.en: MIND AS TERRITORY: an idea can occupy the mind the way a garrison occupies a town.
branches.cn: 心灵即疆域：一个念头占据心灵，正如驻军占据城镇。

intro.en: Occupation is a Latin verb turned into an action noun: a prefix of direction, a root meaning 'seize', and a noun ending that English still uses productively.
intro.cn: occupation 是拉丁动词变来的行为名词：表方向的前缀、意为「抓取」的词根，以及英语仍能产的名称词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere supplies occupy, occupation, occupant, occupancy, capture, captive and capable; ob- adds direction or intensity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 capere 衍生 occupy、occupation、occupant、occupancy、capture、captive 与 capable；ob- 增添方向或强度。

items.example: The prefix directs the action at an object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向某个对象。

items.structure: capere, cepi, captum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root supplies the image of a closed hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「手握紧」的意象。

items.example: Legions could occupy a whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 军团能够占住整条山谷。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成动作的名称。

items.meaning: seizing, holding, or the work one does
items.meaningCN: 占据、持有，或所从事的工作
items.example: The word covers both holding and working.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼指「占住」与「工作」。

items.meaning: to hold or fill a place
items.example: Two families occupy the upper floor.
items.exampleCN: 两户人家住着楼上。

items.example: The occupants left before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 占用者在黎明前离开。

items.example: Occupancy fell after the new road opened.
items.exampleCN: 新路开通后入住率下降。

items.meaningCN: 心事重重的；心不在焉的
items.example: He seemed preoccupied during the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 他在会上显得心不在焉。

definition_zh: 职业的；由工作引起的；与占用有关的
definition_en: relating to a job or profession, or to the conditions and effects of work
core_image: 工厂医务室里，医生对照一张岗位暴露表给工人量血压，窗外是高炉的白烟
scene: 医生翻看工人的岗位记录，判断长期吸入粉尘是否损害了他们的肺。The doctor reviewed the job records to see whether dust exposure had caused occupational lung disease.
sceneCN: 这里 occupational 指「由工作环境引起的」（第 2 个义项：因职业条件导致的疾病或伤害）；句意为医生查阅岗位记录，判断粉尘接触是否造成了职业性肺病。图中可辨识物件：体检表、口罩、听诊器、粉尘采样器。

pos.zh: 职业的；工作引起的；占用相关的

derivatives.zh: 职业；占领；占用（去掉形容词后缀 -al）
在职业方面（-al 加 -ly 构成副词）
作业疗法，用日常活动帮助康复
职业危害，工作本身带来的风险

senses.title: Relating to a person's job
senses.definition: connected with the job or profession a person has
senses.definitionCN: 与某人所从事的职业或工作相关
senses.example: The form asks for occupational history over the past ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 表格要求填写过去十年的职业经历。
senses.why: occupational is simply occupation plus the adjective suffix -al, so it means 'of a job' before anything else.
senses.whyCN: occupational 就是「职业」这一名词加形容词后缀 -al，因此首要意思是「属于职业的」。

senses.title: Caused by conditions at work
senses.definition: caused by the physical or mental conditions of a job
senses.definitionCN: 由工作的身体或心理条件所导致
senses.example: Noise-induced hearing loss is a common occupational injury.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声性听力损失是一种常见的职业伤害。
senses.why: once the adjective was attached to disease and injury, it came to mean 'caused by work' rather than merely 'about work'.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词与疾病、伤害搭配后，意思就从「关于工作」变成「由工作引起」。

senses.title: Relating to the use of premises
senses.definition: connected with the legal or practical holding of a building or land
senses.definitionCN: 与对建筑或土地的法律或实际占用相关
senses.example: The lease sets out the occupational rights of the tenant.
senses.exampleCN: 租约列明了租客的占用权利。
senses.why: the adjective follows the older branch of occupation, where the word means holding premises rather than holding a job.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也跟随这一名词的旧分支，那里的意思是持有房屋而非持有工作。

senses.title: Of therapy based on daily activities
senses.definition: relating to therapy that uses everyday activities to restore function
senses.definitionCN: 与借助日常活动恢复功能的疗法相关
senses.example: After the stroke he began occupational therapy twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 中风后他每周接受两次作业疗法。
senses.why: the therapy is named for the occupations, meaning activities, that patients practise, not for their paid jobs.
senses.whyCN: 这种疗法因患者练习的「日常活动」而得名，并非因他们的有薪工作。

senses.title: Of a surname taken from a trade
senses.titleCN: 以职业为来源的姓氏的
senses.definition: describing a family name derived from an ancestor's trade
senses.definitionCN: 描述由祖先行业演变来的姓氏
senses.example: Smith is the most familiar occupational surname in English.
senses.exampleCN: 史密斯是英语中最常见的职业姓氏。
senses.why: historians of names call surnames occupational when they record what an ancestor did for a living.
senses.whyCN: 姓名学研究把记录祖先谋生行当的姓氏称作职业姓氏。

senses.title: Of job categories in statistics
senses.definition: relating to the grouping of workers by the type of work they do
senses.definitionCN: 与按工作类型对劳动者进行分组相关
senses.example: The survey uses a standard occupational classification.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查采用标准的职业分类。
senses.why: labour statistics needed a neutral adjective for categories of work, and this one filled the gap.
senses.whyCN: 劳动统计需要为工作类别找一个中性的形容词，这个词填补了这一空缺。

senses.title: Of a pension tied to an employer
senses.titleCN: 与雇主挂钩的养老金的
senses.definition: describing a pension provided through a particular job or employer
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过特定工作或雇主提供的养老金
senses.example: She transferred her occupational pension when she changed jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 她换工作时转移了自己的职业养老金。
senses.why: pension law distinguishes schemes tied to an employment from personal ones, and the adjective marks the former.
senses.whyCN: 养老金法规区分与雇佣挂钩的计划与个人计划，这个形容词标出前者。

senses.title: Relating to military occupation
senses.definition: relating to the administration or forces of a territory held by an army
senses.definitionCN: 与军队控制下的地区的管理或部队相关
senses.example: The tribunal examined the occupational authorities' orders.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭审查了占领当局的命令。
senses.why: the adjective also serves the military branch, where occupation means control imposed by force.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词同样服务于军事分支，那里的「占用、职业」指以武力强加的控制。

intro.en: Occupational is an English formation: occupation, from Latin occupatio, plus the adjective suffix -al. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: occupational 是英语构词：occupation 来自拉丁 occupatio，再加形容词后缀 -al。年代均为约数。

items.en: The root capere 'to take, seize' underlies the whole family; its pre-Latin shape is reconstructed, not directly attested.
items.cn: 词根 capere「拿、夺取」支撑整个词族；其拉丁语前形态属于重构形式，并非直接有据。

items.en: Occupatio, from occupare 'seize, hold', named the act of taking possession and later the work that takes up one's time.
items.cn: occupatio 来自 occupare「夺取、持有」，指占有行为，后来也指占去时间的工作。

items.en: English borrowed occupation through Old French in the fourteenth century, and the job sense grew from the idea of time taken up.
items.cn: 英语经古法语在十四世纪借入 occupation，职业义由「时间被占去」这一想法发展而来。

items.en: The Latin adjective suffix -alis, through French -al, was added to make an adjective of 'belonging to occupation'.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 加入，构成表示「属于职业」的形容词。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the adjective was attached to disease, health, therapy and classification, fixing its modern range.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪，这个形容词与疾病、卫生、疗法和分类搭配，固定了它的现代用法范围。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of the adjective is not recorded, and the pre-Latin base of capere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词最早的英语用例没有确切记录，capere 的拉丁语前词基仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin verb and one deceptive look-alike with a different root; group two holds adjectives about work with different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词的词形，外加一个词根不同却形近的词；第二组是范围不同的「工作」形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning a job, a seizure of territory or the use of premises; the adjective adds -al to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指职业、占领领土或占用房屋的名词；形容词是在其后加 -al。

entries.definition: The past participle and adjective meaning in use, taken by an army, or busy; it describes a state, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词兼形容词，意为被占用、被军队占据或忙碌；描述状态而非类别。

entries.definition: The person who occupies a building; it names a person rather than a relation to work.
entries.definitionCN: 指占用某栋建筑的人；指人，而非与工作的关系。

entries.definition: From Latin vocare 'to call', via vocation 'a calling': it means training for a trade, and shares only the ending with occupational.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vocare「召唤」，经 vocation「天职」而来，指职业培训；与 occupational 只共享词尾。

entries.definition: Describing education or training that prepares someone for a specific trade, rather than anything about their current job.
entries.definitionCN: 描述为特定行业做准备的教育或培训，而非关于其现有工作的一切。

entries.definition: Relating to a profession with formal qualifications, and often implying high standards or paid status.
entries.definitionCN: 与具有正式资格的专门职业相关，常暗示高标准或有薪身份。

entries.definition: A plain everyday compound meaning connected with work, without the formal or legal tone of occupational.
entries.definitionCN: 日常朴素的复合词，意为与工作有关，没有 occupational 的正式或法律色彩。

entries.definition: The common spoken equivalent of occupational in phrases such as job-related stress.
entries.definitionCN: 在 job-related stress 一类短语中，是 occupational 的日常口语对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: occupation + -al: the suffix turns the noun into 'relating to'.
normal.cn: occupation 加 -al：后缀把名词变成「与……相关的」。

normal.en: Fixed medical phrases carry the sense: occupational disease, occupational health, occupational therapy.
normal.cn: 固定医学短语承载词义：职业病、职业卫生、作业疗法。

normal.en: The same family gives occupation, occupy, occupant, occupancy, occupier.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 occupation、occupy、occupant、occupancy、occupier。

normal.en: Therapy is occupational because patients practise daily activities, not because they are at work.
normal.cn: 作业疗法之所以叫 occupational，是因为患者练习日常活动，而非因为在上班。

normal.en: Statistics says occupational classification when it groups workers by the type of job.
normal.cn: 统计说 occupational classification 时，是按工作类型给劳动者分类。

abstract.en: Picture a badge that follows a worker from the factory gate to the clinic door.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚徽章跟着工人从厂门一直走到诊所门口。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow cast by a job onto a person's health, long after the shift ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一份工作投在健康上的影子，在下班很久后仍未散去。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a drawer that sorts a whole life by the work written on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉贴着标签，按上面写的工作把一整段人生归类。

examples.en: The clinic specialises in occupational injuries of the hand.
examples.cn: 这家诊所专门治疗手部职业损伤。

examples.en: Occupational mobility is lower in regions with a single large employer.
examples.cn: 在只有一家大型雇主的地区，职业流动性较低。

examples.en: The report compared occupational earnings across five sectors.
examples.cn: 报告比较了五个行业的职业收入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「occupation（职业）+ al（的）」——与职业有关的 → 职业的

root: 拉丁 capere「抓取」→ occupare「夺取、占有」→ occupatio「职业；占据」→ 英语 occupation 加形容词后缀 -al。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all say 'belonging to occupation': to a job, to illness caused by work, to the holding of premises, to therapy by daily activity, to trade surnames, to statistical classes, to employer pensions, and to military rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「属于职业」：属于工作、属于工作引发的疾病、属于房屋的持有、属于日常活动疗法、属于行业姓氏、属于统计类别、属于雇主养老金、属于军事管制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a job casting a long shadow over health, home and paperwork.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份工作把长长的影子投在健康、住所与文书之上。

branches.en: JOB AND CATEGORY: the adjective describes both one person's work and the statistical box it falls into.
branches.cn: 工作与类别：这个形容词既描述某人的工作，也描述它落入的统计格子。

branches.en: WORK AS CAUSE: disease and injury turn 'about work' into 'caused by work'.
branches.cn: 工作作为原因：疾病与伤害把「关于工作」变成「由工作引起」。

branches.en: HOLDING A PLACE: premises held by a tenant and territory held by an army both keep the old sense of occupation.
branches.cn: 占住一处：租客持有的房屋与军队控制的领土，都保留这一名词的旧义。

branches.en: ACTIVITY AS THERAPY: here occupation means the everyday activities a patient practises.
branches.cn: 活动即疗法：这里的「占用、职业」指患者练习的日常活动。

branches.en: INHERITED AND EARNED: a surname records an ancestor's trade, a pension records an employer's scheme.
branches.cn: 承袭与累积：姓氏记录祖先的行业，养老金记录雇主的计划。

intro.en: Occupational is a layered English word: Latin root and prefix, a Latin noun ending, then an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: occupational 是层叠构成的英语词：拉丁词根与前缀、拉丁名词词尾，最后是英语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere 'seize' gives occupare and occupatio; the adjective ending -alis, through French -al, is added in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 capere「抓取」派生 occupare 与 occupatio；形容词词尾 -alis 经法语 -al 在英语中加入。

items.example: The root supplies the sense of grasping.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「抓取」的含义。

items.example: The verb is the base of the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个英语词族的基底。

items.example: The ending forms the noun occupation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成名词 occupation。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表关系的形容词。

items.meaning: relating to a job or to holding a place
items.example: The clinic tracks occupational illness.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所追踪职业病。

items.example: The group is occupationally diverse.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体在职业上很杂。

items.example: Troops occupy the border town.
items.exampleCN: 部队占据边陲小镇。

items.example: The occupant refused to move.
items.exampleCN: 占用者拒绝搬走。

items.example: The occupier pays the water bill.
items.exampleCN: 占用人支付水费。

latinEntries.structure: occupatus, occupata, occupatum (past participle as adjective)

definition_zh: 陶器（总称）；制陶；陶器作坊
definition_en: objects made of fired clay, taken as a group; the craft of making them; a place where they are made
core_image: 转盘上一只湿泥碗慢慢成形，木架上排着刚晾干的坯，地上散落着碎陶片
scene: 考古队在灰坑里挖出许多带纹饰的陶片。The team recovered many decorated pieces of pottery from the refuse pit.
sceneCN: 这里 pottery 指「陶器」（第 1 个义项：用黏土烧制成的器皿总称）；句意为考古队从垃圾坑中取出了许多带纹饰的陶器碎片。图中可辨识物件：陶片、灰坑剖面、刷子、标本袋。

pos.zh: 制陶业；陶器作坊（可数，复数 potteries）

derivatives.zh: 制陶人（pot 加施事后缀 -er）
拉坯轮，制陶用的转盘
陶土，适合拉坯的黏土
陶片，考古断代常用的遗物

senses.title: Fired clay vessels taken as a group
senses.definition: vessels and other objects made of clay and hardened by firing, considered collectively
senses.definitionCN: 用黏土成形并经火烧硬的器皿等物件，作为整体看待
senses.example: The grave contained pottery, beads and a bronze pin.
senses.exampleCN: 墓中有陶器、珠子和一枚铜针。
senses.why: pottery is a mass noun naming the whole class of fired clay ware, so it rarely takes a plural in this sense.
senses.whyCN: pottery 是不可数名词，指烧制陶器这一整类，因此在这个义项中很少用复数。

senses.title: The craft or industry of making pots
senses.definition: the craft or trade of shaping clay into vessels and firing them
senses.definitionCN: 把黏土塑成器皿并烧制的技艺或行业
senses.example: Pottery has been practised in the valley for six centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷制作陶器已有六百年。
senses.why: the activity and its product share one name because English often names a craft by what it turns out.
senses.whyCN: 活动与产物共用一个名称，因为英语常用成品来命名手艺。

senses.title: A workshop where pots are made
senses.definition: a workshop or small studio where clay ware is shaped and fired
senses.definitionCN: 塑形并烧制陶器的工作坊或小工作室
senses.example: She joined a pottery near the harbour to learn glazing.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入港口附近的一家陶艺作坊学习上釉。
senses.why: the suffix -y commonly names a place where an activity is carried on, as in bakery and brewery.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 常命名从事某种活动的地点，如面包房与啤酒厂。

senses.title: Clay ware as archaeological evidence
senses.definition: fired clay objects studied by archaeologists to date and compare cultures
senses.definitionCN: 考古学家用来断代和比较文化的烧制陶器
senses.example: The style of the pottery places the settlement in the late Bronze Age.
senses.exampleCN: 陶器的风格把这处聚落定在青铜时代晚期。
senses.why: because fired clay survives almost everywhere, archaeologists made pottery their standard index of time and culture.
senses.whyCN: 因为烧过的黏土几乎处处都能留存，考古学家把陶器当作时间与文化的标准标尺。

senses.title: A leisure activity or art practice
senses.definition: the activity of making clay objects for pleasure or artistic expression
senses.definitionCN: 为乐趣或艺术表达而制作陶器的活动
senses.example: Pottery became his way of resting after long shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间轮班之后，做陶成了他休息的方式。
senses.why: when the craft moved into studios and evening classes, the same noun came to name the hobby.
senses.whyCN: 当这门手艺进入工作室与夜校课程，同一个名词也开始指这种爱好。

senses.title: A school or college subject
senses.definition: a course of study in which pupils learn to shape and fire clay
senses.definitionCN: 学生学习塑形与烧制黏土的课程
senses.example: Pottery is taught in the same room as woodwork.
senses.exampleCN: 陶艺与木工在同一间教室教授。
senses.why: education borrowed the craft name for the class, as it does with drawing and metalwork.
senses.whyCN: 教育体系借用手艺名称来命名课程，正如绘画课与金工课。

senses.title: Household earthenware as a product class
senses.definition: everyday clay tableware and containers treated as a category of goods
senses.definitionCN: 作为一类商品的日常陶制餐具与容器
senses.example: The shop sells local pottery alongside glass and linen.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店把本地陶器与玻璃器皿、亚麻制品一起出售。
senses.why: retail and industry needed a category label, and pottery supplied the plain mass noun for it.
senses.whyCN: 零售与工业需要一个类别标签，pottery 正好提供了这个朴素的总称。

senses.title: A commercial pot-making works
senses.definition: a commercial works or firm that manufactures clay ware, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 制造陶器的工厂或商号，常用复数
senses.example: The family ran a pottery on the outskirts for three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人曾在城郊经营一家陶器厂，传了三代。
senses.why: the place suffix -y also names a manufactory, so a pottery can be a business rather than a studio.
senses.whyCN: 表地点的后缀 -y 也能命名制造厂，因此 pottery 可以是一家企业而非工作室。

intro.en: Pottery is an English formation from potter plus the place-and-collective suffix -y; potter itself comes from pot with the agent ending -er. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pottery 是英语构词：potter 加表地点与集合的后缀 -y；potter 本身由 pot 加施事后缀 -er 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English pott 'a pot, a vessel' is the base; its deeper Germanic or Latin source is not settled.
items.cn: 古英语 pott「罐、容器」是词基；其更早的日耳曼语或拉丁语来源尚无定论。

items.en: Middle English pottere 'maker of pots' was formed with -er and probably reinforced by Old French potier.
items.cn: 中古英语 pottere「制罐者」由 -er 构成，可能受到古法语 potier 的加强影响。

items.en: The English suffix -y names a place or a collective, as in bakery and brewery, and produced pottery 'the place where pots are made'.
items.cn: 英语后缀 -y 命名地点或集合，如面包房与啤酒厂，由此产生 pottery「制罐之处」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word also named the ware itself, and later the craft and the industry.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词也指器物本身，后来又指手艺与行业。

items.en: Nineteenth-century archaeology made pottery a standard category of finds, which fixed the mass-noun use.
items.cn: 十九世纪考古学把陶器定为标准的一类出土物，从而固定了不可数用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Old-English history of pott is not established, and any reconstructed Germanic form offered for it remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：pott 的古英语之前历史没有定论，为它给出的任何日耳曼语重构形式仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words from different roots, including one that differs by a single letter; group two holds the ceramic terms that are constantly exchanged for pottery.
note.cn: 第一组是词根不同却形近的词，其中一个只差一个字母；第二组是常与 pottery 混用的陶瓷术语。

entries.definition: The maker of pots, formed from pot with the agent suffix -er; pottery is the place or the ware, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 制陶的人，由 pot 加施事后缀 -er 构成；pottery 指地点或器物，不指人。

entries.definition: Domestic birds kept for eggs and meat, from Old French pouletrie; the spelling is close but the root is entirely different.
entries.definitionCN: 为蛋和肉饲养的家禽，来自古法语 pouletrie；拼写相近，但词根完全不同。

entries.definition: A soft paste used for filling holes and holding glass, from French potée; it is not clay ware.
entries.definitionCN: 用于填缝和固定玻璃的软膏，来自法语 potée；并非陶器。

entries.definition: The plain vessel noun from which potter is built; it names one container, not the craft or the ware as a class.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 potter 的朴素容器名词，指单个容器，而非手艺或整类器物。

entries.definition: The art and science of ceramic ware, including porcelain and technical materials; it is the technical umbrella over pottery.
entries.definitionCN: 陶瓷器物制作的艺术与科学，包含瓷器和工业材料；是覆盖 pottery 的技术总称。

entries.definition: Porous clay ware fired at a relatively low temperature, one kind of pottery rather than the whole class.
entries.definitionCN: 较低温度烧成的多孔陶器，是 pottery 中的一种，而非整类。

entries.definition: Dense, vitrified clay ware fired high enough to be waterproof, harder than ordinary earthenware.
entries.definitionCN: 烧成温度足够高、质地致密防水的陶器，比普通陶器坚硬。

entries.definition: Fine white ceramic ware fired at very high temperature, translucent and ringing when struck.
entries.definitionCN: 高温烧成的精细白瓷，半透明，敲击有清脆声。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实复合词与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: pot + -er + -y: a pot maker, then the place or ware associated with that maker.
normal.cn: pot + -er + -y：先有制罐人，再有与制罐人相关的地点或器物。

normal.en: -y as a place suffix appears in bakery and brewery, and the same pattern gives pottery.
normal.cn: -y 作地点后缀见于面包房与啤酒厂，同一模式构成 pottery。

normal.en: Archaeology's standard phrases: pottery shard, decorated pottery, pottery sequence.
normal.cn: 考古学的标准短语：陶片、带纹饰陶器、陶器序列。

normal.en: Everyday use is a mass noun: a piece of pottery, not a pottery.
normal.cn: 日常用法是不可数：说 a piece of pottery，不说 a pottery 指一件。

normal.en: The plural potteries names workshops or firms, not several pieces of ware.
normal.cn: 复数 potteries 指作坊或企业，而不是几件陶器。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl still turning on the wheel, wet and unformed, one minute before it becomes a vessel.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗还在轮上旋转，湿软未定，再过一分钟才成为器皿。

abstract.en: Picture a broken shard that tells an archaeologist more than a whole pot could.
abstract.cn: 想象一块碎陶片，它告诉考古学家的事比一只完整的罐子还多。

abstract.en: Picture hands that have repeated one motion for years until the clay remembers the shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手把同一个动作重复多年，直到泥土记住了形状。

examples.en: The museum displays pottery from three neighbouring villages.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出三个相邻村落的陶器。

examples.en: She took up pottery after she retired.
examples.cn: 她退休后开始做陶。

examples.en: The old pottery by the river now makes tiles for restoration work.
examples.cn: 河边那家老陶器厂如今为修复工程生产瓦件。

root: 古英语 pott「罐」+ 施事后缀 -er → 中古英语 pottere「制罐人」+ 地点后缀 -y → pottery「制陶之处、陶器」。pott 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the fired object to the craft, the workshop, the archaeological index, the hobby, the class, the shop category and finally the factory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从烧成的器物出发，依次走向手艺、作坊、考古标尺、爱好、课程、商品类别，最后是工厂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wet clay on a turning wheel becoming a hard vessel in the fire.
core.cn: 核心意象：转轮上的湿泥在火中变成坚硬的器皿。

branches.en: WARE: fired clay objects, whether studied as a whole class or sold as household goods.
branches.cn: 器物：烧成的陶制品，或作为整类研究，或作为日用商品出售。

branches.en: CRAFT: the skill of shaping and firing, named by the same word as its output.
branches.cn: 手艺：塑形与烧制的技艺，与产物共用同一个词。

branches.en: PLACE: the -y suffix marks a studio workshop and also a commercial works.
branches.cn: 地点：-y 后缀既标出工作室作坊，也标出商业工厂。

branches.en: TIME INDEX: archaeologists read fired clay as a dated signature of culture.
branches.cn: 时间标尺：考古学家把烧过的黏土读作有年代的文化签名。

branches.en: LEARNING AND LEISURE: studios and schools turned the craft into a hobby and a subject.
branches.cn: 学习与闲暇：工作室与学校把这门手艺变成爱好与课程。

intro.en: Pottery is built from English pieces only: a vessel noun, an agent suffix and a place suffix, with no Latin layer in between.
intro.cn: pottery 只由英语成分构成：容器名词、施事后缀与地点后缀，中间没有拉丁层。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin forms are listed; its technical neighbour ceramics comes from Greek instead.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，故不列拉丁词形；它的技术近邻 ceramics 则来自希腊语。

items.example: The base noun names a single vessel.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基名词指单个容器。

items.example: The suffix makes potter out of pot.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 pot 变成 potter。

items.example: The potter shaped the rim with a wet cloth.
items.exampleCN: 制陶人用湿布抹出器口。

items.structure: -y (English suffix for place, collective or activity)
items.example: The same suffix appears in bakery and tannery.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀也见于面包房与制革厂。

items.meaning: a pot-making place; fired clay ware
items.example: The village pottery fired twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 村里的陶窑一年烧两次。

items.meaning: a rotating disc for shaping clay
items.example: The wheel is the potter's chief tool.
items.exampleCN: 转盘是制陶人最主要的工具。

items.example: Local potter's clay is grey and fine-grained.
items.exampleCN: 本地陶土呈灰色，颗粒细。

items.meaning: a fragment of fired clay ware
items.example: A pottery shard lay in the trench floor.
items.exampleCN: 沟底躺着一块陶片。

items.meaning: workshops or firms that make clay ware
items.example: The northern potteries export tableware.
items.exampleCN: 北方的陶器厂出口餐具。

definition_zh: 陶瓷的；陶瓷制品；陶瓷材料
definition_en: made of fired clay or of a similar inorganic material; a ceramic object or material
core_image: 一只上釉的白瓷碗放在灯下，釉面反出冷光，旁边是一片未上釉的灰坯
scene: 工程师把一小片烧成的材料放进高温炉，测试它能否承受骤冷。The engineer placed a ceramic sample in the furnace to test how it survived sudden cooling.
sceneCN: 这里 ceramic 指「陶瓷材料」（第 3 个义项：经高温烧结的无机非金属材料）；句意为工程师把一片陶瓷样品放入炉中，测试它在骤冷后的状态。图中可辨识物件：高温炉、样品夹、温度表、冷却槽。
