senses.title: Made of fired clay
senses.definition: made of clay shaped and hardened by firing
senses.definitionCN: 由黏土塑形并经火烧硬制成的
senses.example: The floor was covered with ceramic tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 地面铺着瓷砖。
senses.why: ceramic is the adjective from the Greek word for potter's clay, so its first job is to describe clay ware.
senses.whyCN: ceramic 是来自希腊语「陶土」一词的形容词，因此首要用途是描述陶制器物。

senses.title: Relating to the ceramic arts
senses.definition: connected with the art and craft of making clay and porcelain objects
senses.definitionCN: 与制作陶器和瓷器的艺术手艺相关
senses.example: The gallery devotes one room to ceramic art.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊用一间展厅陈列陶瓷艺术。
senses.why: museums and studios use the adjective to mark the whole field rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与工作室用这个形容词标注整个领域，而不是单件器物。

senses.title: An engineered inorganic material
senses.definition: a hard, heat-resistant material made by firing inorganic powders, used in engineering
senses.definitionCN: 由无机粉末烧结而成、坚硬耐热的材料，用于工程
senses.example: A ceramic coating protects the turbine blade from heat.
senses.exampleCN: 一层陶瓷涂层保护涡轮叶片免受高温。
senses.why: materials science widened the word from pots to any fired inorganic solid with useful hardness.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学把这个词从陶罐扩展到任何烧成的、具备可用硬度的无机固体。

senses.title: A ceramic object, usually in the plural
senses.definition: an object made of fired clay or porcelain, often spoken of in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 用陶土或瓷土烧成的物件，常以复数形式出现
senses.example: Each ceramic is tested for porosity before packing.
senses.exampleCN: 每件陶瓷制品在包装前都要检测孔隙率。
senses.why: the countable noun turns the material name into one manufactured item.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词用法把材料名转化为一件制成品。

senses.title: Building ware such as tiles and sanitary fittings
senses.definition: fired clay products used in construction, such as tiles, sinks and toilets
senses.definitionCN: 用于建筑的烧制黏土产品，如瓷砖、水槽与便器
senses.example: The bathroom uses ceramic fittings throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室全部使用陶瓷洁具。
senses.why: construction speaks of ceramic rather than pottery because the products are industrial, not artisanal.
senses.whyCN: 建筑行业说「陶瓷」而不说「陶器」，因为这些产品是工业品，不是手工艺品。

senses.title: Material used in dentistry and medicine
senses.definition: a fired inorganic material used for crowns, implants and medical devices
senses.definitionCN: 用于牙冠、植入体与医疗器械的烧制无机材料
senses.example: The crown is made of a translucent ceramic that matches the tooth.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗牙冠用一种与牙齿颜色相近的半透明陶瓷制成。
senses.why: dentistry needed materials that are hard, inert and tooth-coloured, and ceramic supplied all three.
senses.whyCN: 牙科需要坚硬、惰性且颜色接近牙齿的材料，陶瓷正好三者兼具。

senses.title: The glazed surface of such ware
senses.definition: the glassy fired coating on clay ware, considered as a finish
senses.definitionCN: 陶器表面烧成的玻璃质涂层，作为一种饰面
senses.example: A blue ceramic glaze ran down the side of the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 一层蓝色釉顺着碗壁流下。
senses.why: the adjective came to describe the glaze itself, since the finish is what the eye actually sees.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也用来描述釉本身，因为肉眼真正看到的就是这层饰面。

senses.title: Hard plates used in armour
senses.definition: a hard ceramic plate used in protective armour to stop projectiles
senses.definitionCN: 用于防护装甲、阻挡弹丸的硬质陶瓷板
senses.example: The vest carries a ceramic plate over the chest.
senses.exampleCN: 这件防弹背心在胸前装有一块陶瓷板。
senses.why: the engineering sense narrowed again in armour design, where extreme hardness matters more than heat resistance.
senses.whyCN: 工程义在装甲设计中再次收窄，那里极致的硬度比耐热更重要。

intro.en: Ceramic comes from Greek keramikos 'of pottery', from keramos 'potter's clay, pottery', and entered English through learned Latin and French forms in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceramic 来自希腊 keramikos「陶器的」，源于 keramos「陶土、陶器」，十九世纪经学术拉丁语与法语形式进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Keramos named potter's clay and pottery. Its earlier origin is not established; a link to kerannynai 'to mix' is a hypothesis, and a pre-Greek source is also proposed.
items.cn: keramos 指陶土与陶器。其更早来源没有定论；把它联系到 kerannynai「混合」只是假说，也有人提出源自前希腊语。

items.en: Keramikos meant 'of pottery' and was used of the potters' quarter and of clay ware generally.
items.cn: keramikos 意为「陶器的」，用于指陶工区，也泛指陶制器物。

items.en: Learned Latin took the Greek adjective as ceramicus and the noun as ceramica, keeping the Greek root intact.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语把这个希腊形容词写作 ceramicus，名词写作 ceramica，希腊词根原样保留。

items.en: English adopted ceramic in the nineteenth century as the scientific and artistic term for fired clay ware.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪采用 ceramic，作为烧制陶器的科学与艺术术语。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was extended to engineering ceramics, dental ceramics and armour plates.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词扩展到工程陶瓷、牙科陶瓷与装甲板。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of keramos is unsettled, so any older form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：keramos 的前希腊语历史没有定论，为它提出的更早形态均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes with different roots or endings; group two holds the ware names that are often used as if they were synonyms of ceramic.
note.cn: 第一组是词根或词尾不同却形近的词；第二组是常被当作 ceramic 同义词使用的器物名。

entries.definition: The plural noun for the art and science of ceramic ware, or for the objects themselves; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指陶瓷艺术与科学的复数名词，也指器物本身；它不是形容词。

entries.definition: A maker or student of ceramics; the ending marks a person, not a material.
entries.definitionCN: 陶瓷艺人或研究者；词尾标出的是人，不是材料。

entries.definition: The protein of hair, horn and nails, from Greek keras 'horn'; it looks close but has no connection with clay.
entries.definitionCN: 毛发、角与指甲中的蛋白质，来自希腊 keras「角」；形近，但与黏土毫无关系。

entries.definition: A second spelling of the person noun, built with -icist rather than -ist; both are current.
entries.definitionCN: 指人名词的另一种拼法，用 -icist 而非 -ist；两种写法都在使用。

entries.definition: The everyday mass noun for fired clay ware and the craft that makes it; ceramic is its technical and industrial counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指烧制陶器及其手艺的日常名词；ceramic 是它的技术与工业对应词。

entries.definition: Porous clay ware fired at a lower temperature, usually glazed to hold water.
entries.definitionCN: 较低温度烧成的多孔陶器，通常上釉以防渗水。

entries.definition: Dense, non-porous clay ware fired high enough to be waterproof without glaze.
entries.definitionCN: 烧成温度较高、致密不渗水的陶器，无须上釉即可防水。

entries.definition: The finest ceramic ware, white and translucent, fired at very high temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 最精细的陶瓷，白色半透明，烧成温度极高。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real industrial phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构词成分、真实工业短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek keramos 'potter's clay' plus -ic 'relating to': relating to clay ware.
normal.cn: 希腊 keramos「陶土」加 -ic「与……相关」：与陶制器物相关。

normal.en: The family runs ceramic, ceramics, ceramist, ceramicist, ceramically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ceramic、ceramics、ceramist、ceramicist、ceramically。

normal.en: Industry phrases mark the technical sense: advanced ceramic, ceramic coating, ceramic matrix.
normal.cn: 工业短语标出技术义：先进陶瓷、陶瓷涂层、陶瓷基体。

normal.en: Building suppliers speak of ceramic tiles and ceramic fittings, never of pottery tiles.
normal.cn: 建材商说瓷砖与陶瓷洁具，从不说「陶器砖」。

normal.en: Dentistry pairs the word with crown and implant: ceramic crown, ceramic implant.
normal.cn: 牙科把这个词与牙冠、植入体搭配：陶瓷冠、陶瓷植入体。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl so hard that it rings like a bell but shatters like glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗硬得敲起来像钟，却又能像玻璃一样碎裂。

abstract.en: Picture a heat shield that began as a lump of grey powder.
abstract.cn: 想象一块隔热罩，最初只是一团灰色粉末。

abstract.en: Picture a tooth rebuilt from the same stuff as a teacup.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗牙齿用与茶杯相同的材料重建。

examples.en: The façade is clad in ceramic panels that resist graffiti.
examples.cn: 外立面覆以抗涂鸦的陶瓷板。

examples.en: Ceramic bearings run smoothly without oil.
examples.cn: 陶瓷轴承无需润滑油即可平稳运转。

examples.en: The museum bought a set of ceramic vessels from the site.
examples.cn: 博物馆从该遗址购得一套陶瓷器皿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cera（蜡似的光）+ mic」——釉面像蜡一样发亮的东西 → 陶瓷

root: 希腊 keramos「陶土、陶器」→ keramikos「陶器的」→ 学术拉丁 ceramicus → 英语 ceramic。keramos 的更早来源不确定，与前希腊语或 kerannynai「混合」的联系均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from the potter's clay outward: the clay ware itself, the art, the engineered material, one object, building fittings, dental work, the glaze, and finally armour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从陶土向外扩散：陶制器物本身、陶瓷艺术、工程材料、单件制品、建筑洁具、牙科修复、釉面，最后是装甲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft clay passing through fire and coming out hard, glossy and useful.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软的黏土穿过火焰，出来时坚硬、光亮而有用。

branches.en: WARE: the adjective describes fired clay objects, and the countable noun names one of them.
branches.cn: 器物：形容词描述烧制的陶制品，可数名词则指其中一件。

branches.en: SURFACE AND ART: what the eye meets is the glaze, and the craft that produces it is ceramic art.
branches.cn: 表面与艺术：眼睛看到的是釉，制作釉面的手艺就是陶瓷艺术。

branches.en: ENGINEERING HARDNESS: the same material serves turbine blades and armour plates where hardness is the point.
branches.cn: 工程硬度：同一种材料用于涡轮叶片与装甲板，那里关键就是硬度。

branches.en: BUILDING: tiles and sanitary fittings carry the word into construction as an industrial category.
branches.cn: 建筑：瓷砖与洁具把这个词作为工业类别带入建筑业。

branches.en: BODY: dentistry borrows the material because it is hard, inert and close in colour to enamel.
branches.cn: 身体：牙科借用这种材料，因为它坚硬、惰性且颜色接近牙釉质。

intro.en: Ceramic is a Greek root with a Greek adjective ending, routed through learned Latin and then into English.
intro.cn: ceramic 是希腊词根加希腊形容词词尾，经学术拉丁语转入英语。

latinIntro.en: Learned Latin kept the Greek forms as ceramicus and ceramica; English drew ceramic from them and later added -s to make the field name.
latinIntro.cn: 学术拉丁语保留希腊形式写作 ceramicus 与 ceramica；英语由此取得 ceramic，后来又加 -s 构成学科名。

items.example: The root names the material before the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先命名材料，再命名器物。

items.example: The suffix turns the material into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把材料变成形容词。

items.meaning: relating to fired clay; made of it
items.example: A ceramic liner protects the pipe.
items.exampleCN: 陶瓷内衬保护管道。

items.meaning: the field, or a set of objects
items.example: The ending makes ceramics a subject name.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使 ceramics 成为学科名。

items.meaning: the art and science of ceramic ware
items.example: Ceramics is taught in the engineering faculty.
items.exampleCN: 陶瓷学在工学院开设。

items.meaning: a maker or student of ceramics
items.example: The ceramist tested three new glazes.
items.exampleCN: 这位陶艺家试了三种新釉。

items.example: The ceramicist works mainly in porcelain.
items.exampleCN: 这位陶艺家主要用瓷土创作。

items.example: The surface is ceramically bonded.
items.exampleCN: 表面以陶瓷方式结合。

items.meaning: a glassy fired coating on clay ware
items.example: A ceramic glaze sealed the porous body.
items.exampleCN: 一层陶瓷釉封住了多孔的坯体。

senses.title: The art of making ceramic ware
senses.definition: the art and craft of shaping clay and firing it into vessels or figures
senses.definitionCN: 把黏土塑形并烧制成器皿或造型的艺术与手艺
senses.example: She studied ceramics in Kyoto for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在京都学了两年陶瓷。
senses.why: the plural form was taken from the adjective ceramic and used as the name of the whole art.
senses.whyCN: 这个复数形式取自「陶瓷的」这一形容词，被用作整门艺术的名称。

senses.title: Ceramic objects taken as a group
senses.definition: objects made of fired clay or porcelain, considered collectively
senses.definitionCN: 用陶土或瓷土烧成的物件，作为整体看待
senses.example: The tomb yielded ceramics from three different periods.
senses.exampleCN: 这座墓出土了三个不同时期的陶瓷。
senses.why: the ordinary plural of ceramic simply names more than one object, so it doubles as a collective label.
senses.whyCN: 「陶瓷的」这一形容词的普通复数本只表示不止一件器物，因此也兼作集合名称。

senses.title: Engineered ceramic materials
senses.definition: hard, heat-resistant inorganic materials developed for industrial use
senses.definitionCN: 为工业用途开发的坚硬耐热无机材料
senses.example: Advanced ceramics outperform steel in the bearing.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种轴承里，先进陶瓷的性能超过钢材。
senses.why: materials science uses the plural as a mass label for a class of engineered solids.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学用这个复数作为一整类工程固体的不可数标签。

senses.title: The academic discipline or course
senses.definition: the field of study or a taught course concerned with ceramic materials and art
senses.definitionCN: 研究陶瓷材料与艺术的研究领域或开设的课程
senses.example: Ceramics is a required course for conservation students.
senses.exampleCN: 陶瓷学是修复专业学生的必修课。
senses.why: English names many disciplines with a plural ending and a singular verb, as with physics and economics.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用复数词尾配单数动词来命名学科，如物理学与经济学。

senses.title: Ceramic finds studied in archaeology
senses.definition: fired clay objects recovered from sites and used to date and compare cultures
senses.definitionCN: 从遗址出土、用于断代和文化比较的烧制陶器
senses.example: The site's ceramics place it in the Iron Age.
senses.exampleCN: 该遗址的陶瓷把它定在铁器时代。
senses.why: archaeologists shortened 'ceramic objects' to ceramics because fired clay survives and can be classified.
senses.whyCN: 考古学家把「陶瓷器物」简称为 ceramics，因为烧制陶器易于留存且可分类。

senses.title: The ceramics industry
senses.definition: the sector of manufacturing that produces tiles, tableware and technical ceramic goods
senses.definitionCN: 生产瓷砖、餐具与技术陶瓷制品的制造业部门
senses.example: The region's ceramics employ thousands of workers.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的陶瓷工业雇用数千名工人。
senses.why: industry reporting treats the plural as the name of a sector, like textiles or plastics.
senses.whyCN: 产业报道把这个复数当作部门名称，如同纺织业与塑料业。

senses.title: Dental and medical ceramics
senses.definition: ceramic materials used to rebuild teeth or to make medical implants
senses.definitionCN: 用于修复牙齿或制造医疗植入体的陶瓷材料
senses.example: Modern dentistry relies on ceramics for crowns.
senses.exampleCN: 现代牙科依靠陶瓷制作牙冠。
senses.why: dentists use the plural as a material category because several ceramic systems are in use.
senses.whyCN: 牙医使用这个复数作为材料类别，因为在用的陶瓷体系不止一种。

senses.title: Glazes and protective ceramic layers
senses.definition: glassy or ceramic coatings applied to a surface for protection or decoration
senses.definitionCN: 为保护或装饰而施加于表面的玻璃质或陶瓷涂层
senses.example: The engine runs hotter because its ceramics insulate the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 由于陶瓷层隔热，这台发动机能在更高温度下运转。
senses.why: coatings are ceramic too, so the plural extends from solid ware to thin protective layers.
senses.whyCN: 涂层同样是陶瓷，因此这个复数从实体器物扩展到薄薄的保护层。

intro.en: Ceramics is the English plural of ceramic, from Greek keramikos 'of pottery', and was adopted in the nineteenth century as the name of the art and science. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceramics 是 ceramic 的英语复数，源自希腊 keramikos「陶器的」，在十九世纪被采用为这门艺术与科学的名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: Keramos meant potter's clay and pottery; its deeper origin is uncertain, and both a pre-Greek source and a link to kerannynai 'to mix' are hypotheses.
items.cn: keramos 指陶土与陶器；其更深来源不确定，源自前希腊语与联系到 kerannynai「混合」都只是假说。

items.en: The adjective keramikos 'of pottery' described clay ware and the potters' quarter of Athens.
items.cn: 形容词 keramikos「陶器的」用于描述陶制器物，也指雅典的陶工区。

items.en: Learned Latin used ceramica as a noun for pottery, keeping the Greek root that English later borrowed.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语用 ceramica 作为「陶器」的名词，保留了英语后来借用的希腊词根。

items.en: Nineteenth-century English adopted ceramic as the technical term, and the plural ceramics became the name of the field.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语采用 ceramic 作为技术术语，其复数 ceramics 成为该领域的名称。

items.en: Twentieth-century engineering extended ceramics to advanced materials, coatings and medical implants.
items.cn: 二十世纪工程学把 ceramics 扩展到先进材料、涂层与医用植入体。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of keramos is not settled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：keramos 的前希腊语历史尚无定论，为它提出的更早形态均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that differ only by an ending but belong to different word classes; group two holds ware names that are not interchangeable with ceramics.
note.cn: 第一组只差词尾、却属于不同词类的词形；第二组是不可与 ceramics 随意互换的器物名称。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of fired clay' or a singular countable object; ceramics is the field or the mass of objects.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「陶制的」的形容词，或单件可数制品；ceramics 则是学科或器物总称。

entries.definition: A person who makes or studies ceramics; the ending -ist marks a person, not a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或研究陶瓷的人；词尾 -ist 标出人，而非学科。

entries.definition: A rival formation for the same person noun, built on ceramic plus -ist rather than on ceram-.
entries.definitionCN: 同一指人名词的另一种构法，在 ceramic 上加 -ist，而非在 ceram- 上加。

entries.definition: The protein of hair and nails, from Greek keras 'horn'; the resemblance to ceramics is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 毛发与指甲中的蛋白质，来自希腊 keras「角」；与 ceramics 的相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: The everyday word for fired clay ware and its craft; ceramics is the technical and industrial umbrella.
entries.definitionCN: 指烧制陶器及其手艺的日常词；ceramics 是技术与工业上的总称。

entries.definition: Porous, low-fired clay ware, usually glazed; it is one category within ceramics.
entries.definitionCN: 多孔、低温烧成的陶器，通常上釉；是 ceramics 中的一个类别。

entries.definition: Dense, waterproof clay ware fired at a higher temperature; another single category.
entries.definitionCN: 较高温度烧成、致密防水的陶器；同属单一类别。

entries.definition: White, translucent high-fired ware; the most refined product within ceramics.
entries.definitionCN: 白色半透明的高温瓷器；是 ceramics 中最精细的产品。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real course and industry phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实课程与产业短语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ceramic plus -s: the plural ending turns an adjective into a field name, as with physics.
normal.cn: ceramic 加 -s：复数词尾把形容词变成学科名，如同物理学。

normal.en: The subject takes a singular verb: ceramics is taught here.
normal.cn: 这个学科名接单数动词：陶瓷学在这里教授。

normal.en: Industry phrases mark the material sense: advanced ceramics, technical ceramics.
normal.cn: 产业短语标出材料义：先进陶瓷、技术陶瓷。

normal.en: The family runs ceramic, ceramics, ceramist, ceramicist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ceramic、ceramics、ceramist、ceramicist。

normal.en: Archaeology says the site's ceramics when it means the pots found there.
normal.cn: 考古学用 the site's ceramics 指在那里发现的陶器。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of pots that becomes a library of dates.
abstract.cn: 想象一排陶罐变成一座年代图书馆。

abstract.en: Picture a craft that splits into an art studio and a factory floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一门手艺分成艺术工作室与工厂车间。

abstract.en: Picture a discipline with a singular name built from a plural ending.
abstract.cn: 想象一门学科，名字由复数词尾构成，却按单数使用。

examples.en: The museum's ceramics gallery reopened after restoration.
examples.cn: 博物馆的陶瓷展厅修复后重新开放。

examples.en: Ceramics is taught alongside glassblowing in the craft school.
examples.cn: 这所工艺学校把陶瓷与吹玻璃一起教授。

examples.en: The firm supplies ceramics for jet engine components.
examples.cn: 这家公司为喷气发动机部件供应陶瓷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ceramic（陶瓷的）+ s」——陶瓷这门学问与这批器物 → 陶瓷工艺

root: 希腊 keramos「陶土」→ keramikos「陶器的」→ 拉丁 ceramica「陶器」→ 英语 ceramic 加 -s 构成学科名 ceramics。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the studio to the factory: the art, the objects, engineered materials, the course, the dig, the industry, the clinic and the coating.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从工作室走到工厂：艺术、器物、工程材料、课程、考古发掘、产业、诊所与涂层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one craft splitting into art, science and industry while keeping the same clay at its base.
core.cn: 核心意象：一门手艺分化为艺术、科学与工业，底部仍是同一种黏土。

branches.en: ART AND STUDY: the same plural names a studio art and a taught discipline with a singular verb.
branches.cn: 艺术与学问：同一个复数既指工作室艺术，也指接单数动词的学科。

branches.en: OBJECTS: whole collections and excavated finds are both called ceramics.
branches.cn: 器物：整批藏品与出土遗物都被称作 ceramics。

branches.en: MATERIALS: engineered solids and thin protective coatings share the ceramic base.
branches.cn: 材料：工程固体与薄保护层共享陶瓷基底。

branches.en: SECTOR: the plural becomes the name of an industry, like textiles or plastics.
branches.cn: 产业：这个复数成为一个行业名称，如同纺织业与塑料业。

branches.en: CLINIC: dental and medical ceramics apply the material to the body.
branches.cn: 诊所：牙科与医用陶瓷把这种材料用于身体。

intro.en: Ceramics is the Greek clay root plus a Greek adjective ending plus an English plural used as a subject name.
intro.cn: ceramics 由希腊陶土词根、希腊形容词词尾，再加用作学科名的英语复数构成。

latinIntro.en: Learned Latin kept the Greek forms ceramicus and ceramica; English took ceramic from them and added -s for the field.
latinIntro.cn: 学术拉丁语保留希腊形式 ceramicus 与 ceramica；英语由此取得 ceramic，并加 -s 表示学科。

items.example: The root names the material of the craft.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名这门手艺的材料。

items.example: The suffix forms the adjective ceramic.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成形容词 ceramic。

items.example: The tile is ceramic, not stone.
items.exampleCN: 这块砖是陶制的，不是石头的。

items.meaning: a set, or a named field
items.example: The ending names both objects and the subject.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾既指器物，也指学科。

items.meaning: the art and science of ceramic ware
items.example: Ceramics is her major.
items.exampleCN: 陶瓷学是她的专业。

items.example: The ceramist built the vase by hand.
items.exampleCN: 这位陶艺家手工捏成花瓶。

items.example: A ceramicist judged the student show.
items.exampleCN: 一位陶艺家评审学生作品展。

items.example: The layers are ceramically bonded.
items.exampleCN: 各层以陶瓷方式结合。

items.example: Technical ceramics resist wear at high speed.
items.exampleCN: 技术陶瓷在高速下耐磨损。

definition_en: a heated chamber or oven used to fire clay, dry timber or burn lime; to fire something in such a chamber
core_image: 山坡上隆起的砖砌窑体，烟从顶部小孔冒出，窑口透出橙红色的光
scene: 制陶人整夜守在窑口，火一弱就添柴。The potter watched the kiln all night, adding wood whenever the fire dimmed.
sceneCN: 这里 kiln 指「烧制陶器的窑」（第 1 个义项：用于烧硬陶坯的封闭炉体）；句意为制陶人整夜守着窑，火势减弱时就添柴。图中可辨识物件：砖砌窑体、烟孔、柴堆、火钩。

pos.zh: 把……放入窑中烧制或烘干

derivatives.zh: 入窑烧制；窑烘过程（-ing 构成动名词）
窑干的（复合形容词）
石灰窑（lime 加 kiln 的复合词）
看窑工（行业用语）

senses.title: An oven for firing pottery
senses.definition: a closed chamber heated to a high temperature so that clay ware hardens
senses.definitionCN: 加热到高温、使陶坯硬化的封闭炉室
senses.example: The workshop fires its bowls in a wood kiln.
senses.exampleCN: 作坊用柴窑烧碗。
senses.why: the word's oldest surviving sense is a heated chamber, and pottery firing is the use that kept it alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词现存最古老的义项是「加热的炉室」，而烧陶是让它延续下来的用途。

senses.title: An oven for lime, brick or charcoal
senses.definition: a heated chamber used to burn limestone, fire bricks or make charcoal
senses.definitionCN: 用于烧石灰石、烧砖或制炭的加热炉室
senses.example: The lime kiln at the quarry closed in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 采石场的石灰窑在上个世纪关闭了。
senses.why: before it meant pottery, the word covered any heated chamber, and these older industries kept that breadth.
senses.whyCN: 在指陶窑之前，这个词泛指任何加热炉室，这些更古老的行业保留了这一广度。

senses.title: To fire something in a kiln
senses.definition: to dry or fire an object in a kiln
senses.definitionCN: 把物件放入窑中烘干或烧制
senses.example: They kiln the greenware slowly to prevent cracks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们慢慢把素坯入窑烧制，以防开裂。
senses.why: English readily turns a container noun into a verb meaning 'put into that container'.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把容器名词转为动词，表示「放进该容器」。

senses.title: An industrial drier for timber
senses.definition: a heated chamber in which sawn timber is dried under controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在受控条件下烘干锯材的加热炉室
senses.example: The planks spend three weeks in the kiln.
senses.exampleCN: 这些板材要在烘干窑里待三周。
senses.why: timber drying borrowed the pottery word because the chamber and the controlled heat are the same.
senses.whyCN: 木材干燥借用了陶窑的词，因为炉室与受控加热是一回事。

senses.title: A continuous tunnel kiln
senses.definition: a long tunnel furnace in which ware moves continuously through zones of increasing heat
senses.definitionCN: 器物连续穿过温度递增各段的长隧道式炉
senses.example: A tunnel kiln fires thousands of tiles a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一条隧道窑每天烧制数千块砖。
senses.why: industrial scale replaced the single chamber with a tunnel, but kept the old name.
senses.whyCN: 工业规模把单间炉室换成隧道，却沿用了旧名。

senses.title: An oast for drying hops
senses.definition: a heated building in which hops are dried after harvest
senses.definitionCN: 收获后用来烘干啤酒花的加热建筑
senses.example: The conical kiln beside the brewery is now a house.
senses.exampleCN: 酿酒厂旁那座锥顶烘干房如今成了一户住宅。
senses.why: the same need, controlled heat, gave the drying house its local name in brewing regions.
senses.whyCN: 同样的需求，即受控加热，让烘干房在酿酒地区得到这个本地名称。

senses.title: A place of intense heat, figuratively
senses.definition: a place or situation imagined as a furnace of unbearable heat
senses.definitionCN: 被想象成难以忍受的炙热炉膛的处所或处境
senses.example: At noon the valley becomes a kiln.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时分，山谷成了一座窑。
senses.why: the closed, glowing chamber is a ready image for any heat that seems to have no outlet.
senses.whyCN: 封闭发光的炉室很容易被用来比喻任何仿佛无处散出的酷热。

senses.title: A rotary kiln in cement making
senses.definition: a long rotating cylinder in which cement raw meal is heated and fused
senses.definitionCN: 水泥生料在其中受热并烧结的长旋转筒
senses.example: The rotary kiln turns limestone and clay into clinker.
senses.exampleCN: 回转窑把石灰石与黏土烧成熟料。
senses.why: cement making adopted the name for its central furnace, extending it to one of the largest machines in industry.
senses.whyCN: 水泥制造为其核心炉采用这个名称，把它扩展为工业中最大的机械之一。

intro.en: Kiln is an Old English word, recorded as cylene, borrowed from Latin culina 'kitchen, cookstove'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: kiln 是古英语词，写作 cylene，借自拉丁 culina「厨房、炉灶」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Culina meant 'kitchen, cookstove'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to coquere 'to cook' has been suggested but is not demonstrated.
items.cn: culina 意为「厨房、炉灶」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出与 coquere「烹煮」有关，但未得到证明。

items.en: Old English cylene was borrowed from the Latin word and meant a heated chamber or oven, not specifically a kitchen.
items.cn: 古英语 cylene 借自这个拉丁词，指加热的炉室或烤炉，并不专指厨房。

items.en: The Middle English form settled as kilne, later kiln, with the meaning narrowing toward a furnace for firing or drying.
items.cn: 中古英语形式定型为 kilne，后作 kiln，词义收窄为烧制或烘干的炉。

items.en: Pottery, lime, brick and charcoal making each kept the word for their own furnace, and timber drying joined them.
items.cn: 制陶、烧灰、制砖与烧炭各自用这个词指自己的炉，木材烘干随后加入。

items.en: The n is often not pronounced, so the word commonly sounds like kil, though the spelling keeps the older form.
items.cn: 词尾的 n 常不发音，因此这个词听起来常像 kil，但拼写保留了较古老的形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of culina is not established, and the suggested connection with coquere remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：culina 的拉丁语之前历史没有定论，与 coquere 的联系仍属假说。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes and derivatives that are easy to confuse with the noun; group two holds the heating devices that are not kilns.
note.cn: 第一组是易与名词混淆的形近词与派生词；第二组是不是窑的加热设备。

entries.definition: To cause death, from a Germanic verb; it sounds almost the same as the spoken kiln but has no relation.
entries.definitionCN: 意为致死，来自日耳曼语动词；与口语中的 kiln 读音几乎相同，却毫无关系。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of the verb, meaning dried or fired in a kiln, as in kilned malt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词，意为在窑中烘干或烧制，如窑干麦芽。

entries.definition: The process of firing or drying in a kiln; the -ing form names the activity, not the building.
entries.definitionCN: 在窑中烧制或烘干的过程；-ing 形式指活动，不指建筑。

entries.definition: A compound of lime plus kiln, naming the furnace where limestone is burned; it is a type of kiln, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 由 lime 加 kiln 构成的复合词，指烧石灰的炉；是窑的一种，并非另一词根。

entries.definition: An enclosed chamber for cooking or heating food, usually in a kitchen; kiln is for materials, not meals.
entries.definitionCN: 厨房中烹饪或加热食物的封闭炉室；kiln 用于材料，不用于饭菜。

entries.definition: A very hot chamber for burning fuel or melting materials; it stresses intense heat rather than the product fired.
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧燃料或熔化材料的极热炉室；强调高温，而非所烧制的产品。

entries.definition: A device for cooking or heating a room, typically domestic and fuelled for daily use.
entries.definitionCN: 用于烹饪或取暖的设备，通常为家用且日常燃料驱动。

entries.definition: A building for drying hops, the brewing-specific equivalent of a kiln.
entries.definitionCN: 烘干啤酒花的建筑，是酿酒业中专用的窑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real industry terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实复合词、真实行业术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Borrowed from Latin culina 'kitchen', so a kiln began as a hearth and became a furnace.
normal.cn: 借自拉丁 culina「厨房」，因此窑最初是灶，后来成了炉。

normal.en: Compounds name what is fired: brick kiln, lime kiln, charcoal kiln.
normal.cn: 复合词说明烧的是什么：砖窑、石灰窑、炭窑。

normal.en: Kiln-dried is a standard label on timber and malt.
normal.cn: kiln-dried 是木材与麦芽上的标准标签。

normal.en: The n is silent in speech: say kil, spell kiln.
normal.cn: 口语中 n 不发音：说 kil，拼作 kiln。

normal.en: The verb works both ways: they kiln the greenware, the malt is kilned.
normal.cn: 动词可主动可被动：他们把素坯入窑，麦芽被窑烘。

abstract.en: Picture a small brick hill with a star of fire inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座砖砌的小山，里面藏着一团星形的火。

abstract.en: Picture a tunnel long enough that ware enters soft and leaves ringing.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长隧道，器物软着进去，出来时敲之有声。

abstract.en: Picture noon in a valley where the air itself seems fired.
abstract.cn: 想象山谷的正午，连空气都像被烧过。

examples.en: The kiln must cool for a full day before the door is opened.
examples.cn: 窑要冷却一整天才能开门。

examples.en: They kiln the malt over oak logs.
examples.cn: 他们用橡木柴烘麦芽。

examples.en: Bricks from the old kiln were reused in the garden wall.
examples.cn: 老砖窑的砖被重新用在花园墙上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「kiln」读音近「kill」——把泥坯放进高温里「定」下来 → 窑

root: 拉丁 culina「厨房、炉灶」→ 古英语 cylene「加热炉室」→ 中古英语 kilne → 现代 kiln。culina 更深来源不确定，与 coquere「烹煮」的联系属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one heated chamber: pots, lime and bricks, the act of firing, timber, the tunnel version, hops, a metaphor for heat, and the cement rotary kiln.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个加热炉室展开：陶器、石灰与砖、入窑烧制、木材、隧道式窑、啤酒花、酷热的比喻，以及水泥回转窑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed brick chamber holding fire long enough to change what is inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间封闭的砖砌炉室，把火留住足够久，使里面的东西改变。

branches.en: POTTERY AND ITS VERB: the potter's chamber and the act of putting ware into it.
branches.cn: 陶窑与其动词：制陶人的炉室，以及把陶坯放进去的动作。

branches.en: OTHER CRAFT FIRES: lime, brick, charcoal and hops each kept the name for their own heated chamber.
branches.cn: 其他行业的火：石灰、砖、炭与啤酒花各自用这个词指自己的加热炉室。

branches.en: SCALE: timber drying and the continuous tunnel show the word moving from craft to industry.
branches.cn: 规模：木材烘干与连续隧道显示这个词从手艺走向工业。

branches.en: CEMENT: the rotary kiln is the largest descendant of the same chamber.
branches.cn: 水泥：回转窑是同一炉室最大的后裔。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any unbearable heat can be pictured as a kiln.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何难以忍受的酷热都可以被想象成一座窑。

intro.en: Kiln is a borrowed Latin noun reshaped by Old English; it carries no productive prefix or suffix of its own, but it builds compounds freely.
intro.cn: kiln 是经古英语改造的拉丁借词；它本身不带能产的前后缀，却能自由构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin culina 'kitchen' is the source; the Latin noun culina and its adjective culinarius survive in English culinary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 culina「厨房」是来源；拉丁名词 culina 与其形容词 culinarius 仍活在英语 culinary 中。

items.example: The Latin noun is the remote source of kiln.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是 kiln 的远源。

items.example: The old kiln still stands by the orchard.
items.exampleCN: 老窑仍立在果园旁。

items.example: Two kilns serve the whole village.
items.exampleCN: 两座窑供应整个村子。

items.example: The malt was kilned last week.
items.exampleCN: 麦芽上周已窑烘。

items.example: Kilning takes four days here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的窑烘要四天。

items.example: Kiln-dried oak is stable enough for doors.
items.exampleCN: 窑干橡木做门足够稳定。

items.example: The brick kiln fired a million bricks a year.
items.exampleCN: 这座砖窑一年烧一百万块砖。

items.example: The limekiln closed when the quarry shut.
items.exampleCN: 采石场关闭时石灰窑也停了。

items.meaning: a worker who tends a kiln
items.example: The kilnman judged the fire by its colour.
items.exampleCN: 看窑工凭火色判断火候。

latinEntries.meaning: to cook (offered only as a possible link, not a proven source)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 烹煮（仅作为一种可能的联系，并非已证来源）

definition_en: a three-dimensional work of art made by shaping or carving material; the art of making such works
core_image: 工作室中央立着一块尚未完成的大理石人像，肩上落满石粉，四周是锤子和凿子
scene: 美术馆把一座青铜人像安放在中庭，观众可以绕着它走一圈。The gallery placed a bronze sculpture in the courtyard so visitors could walk around it.
sceneCN: 这里 sculpture 指「雕塑作品」（第 1 个义项：三维立体造型艺术品）；句意为美术馆把一件青铜雕塑放在中庭，让观众可以绕行观看。图中可辨识物件：青铜人像、基座、天窗、参观者。

pos.zh: 雕塑；雕刻成形（较少用，常用「雕刻」这一动词形式）

derivatives.zh: 雕塑；造型（由名词截短而来）
雕塑家（-or 表施事者）
雕塑的；具雕塑感的
雕刻成的；有立体造型的

senses.title: A three-dimensional work of art
senses.definition: a work of art made by shaping, carving or casting material in three dimensions
senses.definitionCN: 通过塑形、雕刻或铸造材料而成的三维艺术品
senses.example: The bronze sculpture dominates the entrance hall.
senses.exampleCN: 那件青铜雕塑占据了入口大厅。
senses.why: sculpture comes from Latin sculptura 'a carving', so the object and the act were one word from the start.
senses.whyCN: sculpture 来自拉丁 sculptura「雕刻物」，因此物件与动作从一开始就共用一个词。

senses.title: The art of making such works
senses.definition: the art or practice of making three-dimensional forms
senses.definitionCN: 制作三维造型的艺术或实践
senses.example: He turned from painting to sculpture at thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十岁时从绘画转向雕塑。
senses.why: the uncountable use names the discipline, just as painting names an art rather than one canvas.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法命名这门学科，正如「绘画」命名一门艺术而非一幅画。

senses.title: A single carved or cast figure
senses.definition: one figure or object carved, modelled or cast from stone, metal or wood
senses.definitionCN: 用石、金属或木料雕成、塑成或铸成的一件形象或器物
senses.example: A marble sculpture of a hand rests on the plinth.
senses.exampleCN: 一只大理石手部雕塑放在基座上。
senses.why: the countable use treats the art object as one item among many in a collection.
senses.whyCN: 可数用法把这件艺术品当作收藏中的一件。

senses.title: To shape material into a figure
senses.definition: to shape or carve material into a three-dimensional form
senses.definitionCN: 把材料雕琢或塑造成三维形体
senses.example: The artist sculptured the figure from a single block.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术家用一整块石料雕出这个人物。
senses.why: the verb is simply the noun put to work, and modern English often prefers the shorter sculpt.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词直接用作动作，现代英语更常用更短的动词形式。

senses.title: A natural form that looks carved
senses.titleCN: 天然形成的雕塑状地貌
senses.definition: a rock or landform whose shape seems deliberately modelled
senses.definitionCN: 形状仿佛经刻意塑形的岩石或地貌
senses.example: Wind and salt have made a sculpture of the coastal rock.
senses.exampleCN: 风与盐把海岸岩石雕成了一件作品。
senses.why: the word extends to nature whenever erosion produces something that looks made by a sculptor.
senses.whyCN: 当侵蚀造出仿佛雕塑家所做的形状时，这个词就扩展到自然。

senses.title: Raised carving on a flat surface
senses.definition: carving in which figures are raised from a flat background, as on a frieze
senses.definitionCN: 形象从平面背景凸出的雕刻，如横饰带上的浮雕
senses.example: A relief sculpture of dancers runs along the frieze.
senses.exampleCN: 一条横饰带上有一列舞者的浮雕。
senses.why: relief is sculpture still attached to its block, and English names it by adding the qualifier relief.
senses.whyCN: 浮雕仍是连着石块的雕塑，英语加「浮雕」这一限定词来命名。

senses.title: A public monument
senses.definition: a large outdoor work, often commemorative, placed in a public space
senses.definitionCN: 置于公共空间的大型户外作品，常具纪念性
senses.example: The city unveiled a sculpture honouring the dock workers.
senses.exampleCN: 该市为纪念码头工人揭幕了一座雕塑。
senses.why: public art made sculpture a civic object, so the word now also names monuments by its own name.
senses.whyCN: 公共艺术使雕塑成为城市物件，于是这个词也直接用来指纪念碑。

senses.title: An ephemeral work such as ice sculpture
senses.definition: a temporary work made of melting or fragile material, created for an event
senses.definitionCN: 为活动而作、用易融或易碎材料制成的临时作品
senses.example: The ice sculpture melted before the speeches ended.
senses.exampleCN: 冰雕在致辞结束前就融化了。
senses.why: because the definition depends on three-dimensional shaping rather than permanence, ice and sand qualify.
senses.whyCN: 因为定义取决于三维塑形而非永久性，冰与沙也符合条件。

intro.en: Sculpture comes from Latin sculptura 'a carving', from sculpere 'to carve, cut out'. English took it through French and Italian forms in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sculpture 来自拉丁 sculptura「雕刻物」，源自动词 sculpere「雕刻、削出」。英语在十六世纪经法语与意大利语形式借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sculpere meant 'to carve, cut out, shape by cutting'. It is generally connected with the idea of cutting, and related forms appear in scalprum 'a chisel'.
items.cn: sculpere 意为「雕刻、削出、以切削成形」。一般认为它与「切」这一概念相关，相关形态见于 scalprum「凿子」。

items.en: The noun sculptura named both the act of carving and the carved object, a double sense English inherited.
items.cn: 名词 sculptura 兼指雕刻动作与雕刻成品，英语继承了这个双重含义。

items.en: Renaissance Italian scultura and French sculpture carried the word into English, where it settled in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的意大利语 scultura 与法语 sculpture 把这个词带入英语，十六世纪定型。

items.en: Stone, bronze, wood and clay were all covered, with casting treated as sculpture as much as carving.
items.cn: 石、青铜、木与黏土都包括在内，铸造与雕刻同样被视为雕塑。

items.en: Public monuments and modern temporary works widened the word beyond gallery pieces.
items.cn: 公共纪念碑与现代临时作品把这个词扩展到画廊作品之外。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin base of sculpere is reconstructed, and its exact relation to scalprum and to the cutting family is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：sculpere 的拉丁语前词基属于重构形式，它与 scalprum 及「切」词族的确切关系仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds the word's own family and one scalpel look-alike from the same cutting stock; group two holds kinds of three-dimensional work that are not synonyms of sculpture.
note.cn: 第一组是这个词自身的词族，外加一个同出「切」词族的形近词；第二组是并非 sculpture 同义词的三维作品类别。

entries.definition: The artist who makes sculpture, formed with the agent ending -or; it names a person, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 制作雕塑的艺术家，用施事后缀 -or 构成；指人，不指作品。

entries.definition: The clipped modern verb meaning to make a sculpture, more common than sculpture as a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 截短而来的现代动词，意为制作雕塑，作动词时比 sculpture 更常用。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of sculpture' or 'like sculpture'; it describes a quality, not an object.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「雕塑的」或「像雕塑的」形容词；描述性质，不指物件。

entries.definition: A small surgical knife, from Latin scalprum 'chisel'; it shares the cutting idea with sculpture but is not the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 外科小刀，来自拉丁 scalprum「凿子」；与 sculptura 共享「切」的概念，但并非同一个词。

entries.definition: A carved or cast figure of a person or animal, usually life-size or larger; it is one kind of sculpture.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物的雕铸形象，通常与真人等大或更大；是雕塑的一种。

entries.definition: An object or design cut into wood or stone; it stresses the cutting process and often decoration rather than free-standing art.
entries.definitionCN: 在木石上刻出的物件或纹样；强调切削过程，常指装饰而非独立艺术品。

entries.definition: Carving whose figures stand out from a flat background; it is sculpture still attached to its block.
entries.definitionCN: 形象从平面背景凸出的雕刻；仍是连着石块的雕塑。

entries.definition: A sculpture of a person's head and shoulders, a subtype defined by what it shows.
entries.definitionCN: 人像头部与肩部的雕塑，按所表现的范围界定的一种类型。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real museum phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实博物馆短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin sculpere 'carve' plus -ura gives sculpture: the carved thing and the carving act.
normal.cn: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻」加 -ura 构成 sculpture：既是刻成之物，也是雕刻动作。

normal.en: The family runs sculpt, sculptor, sculpture, sculptural, sculptured.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sculpt、sculptor、sculpture、sculptural、sculptured。

normal.en: Museum labels mark the types: bronze sculpture, marble sculpture, relief sculpture.
normal.cn: 博物馆标签标出类型：青铜雕塑、大理石雕塑、浮雕。

normal.en: Relief sculpture is still attached to its background; free-standing sculpture is not.
normal.cn: 浮雕仍连着背景；独立雕塑则否。

normal.en: Ice sculpture shows that the word needs shaping, not permanence.
normal.cn: 冰雕说明这个词需要的是塑形，而非永久。

abstract.en: Picture a block of stone that has one figure hidden inside it and one way to get it out.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头里藏着一个形象，只有一条路能把它取出来。

abstract.en: Picture a person walking around a figure and seeing a different work from every side.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人绕着雕像走，每换一面就看到一件不同的作品。

abstract.en: Picture a shape that exists only for one afternoon before the sun takes it back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个形状只存在一个下午，随后被太阳收回。

examples.en: The sculpture weighs more than a small car.
examples.cn: 这件雕塑比一辆小汽车还重。

examples.en: She teaches sculpture at the art school.
examples.cn: 她在艺术学校教雕塑。

examples.en: The park holds a sculpture made of weathered steel.
examples.cn: 公园里有一件用耐候钢制成的雕塑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sculpt（雕刻）+ ure」——刻出来的东西 → 雕塑

root: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻、削出」→ sculptura「雕刻物、雕刻」→ 经意大利语与法语进入英语 sculpture。sculpere 的拉丁语前词基为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from one carved object to the art itself, then to natural rock, relief, public monuments and ice that melts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一件刻成的物件走向艺术本身，再走向天然岩石、浮雕、公共纪念碑与会融化的冰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure released from a block by cutting away everything that is not the figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：把不是形象的部分全部削去，让形象从石块中脱出。

branches.en: OBJECT: one three-dimensional work and one carved figure are the countable core of the word.
branches.cn: 物件：一件三维作品与一件雕成形象，是这个词可数的核心。

branches.en: ART AND ACT: the discipline and the verb both name the shaping of material.
branches.cn: 艺术与动作：学科与动词都命名对材料的塑形。

branches.en: NATURE: erosion can produce what looks like deliberate carving.
branches.cn: 自然：侵蚀能造出仿佛刻意雕出的形状。

branches.en: ATTACHED AND PUBLIC: relief stays on its wall, while monuments stand free in civic space.
branches.cn: 附着与公共：浮雕留在墙上，纪念碑则独立于城市空间。

branches.en: TEMPORARY: ice shows that shaping, not lasting, defines the word.
branches.cn: 临时：冰雕说明定义这个词的是塑形，而非长久。

intro.en: Sculpture is a Latin verb plus a Latin result suffix, with an English agent noun and adjective built on the same stem.
intro.cn: sculpture 是拉丁动词加拉丁结果后缀，同一词干上还构成英语施事名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sculpere 'carve' gives sculptura, sculptor and sculptilis; the same cutting idea appears in scalprum 'chisel'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻」衍生 sculptura、sculptor 与 sculptilis；同样的「切」意也见于 scalprum「凿子」。

items.example: The root carries the act of cutting away.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「削去」的动作。

items.meaning: the result or act of an action
items.meaningCN: 动作的结果或动作本身
items.example: The suffix forms the noun of result.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成结果名词。

items.meaning: a carving; the art of carving
items.example: The Latin noun already held both senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已兼含两义。

items.meaning: three-dimensional art or a work of it
items.example: The sculpture is cast in bronze.
items.exampleCN: 这件雕塑以青铜铸成。

items.example: The sculptor worked only at night.
items.exampleCN: 这位雕塑家只在夜里工作。

items.structure: sculpture clipped to a verb stem
items.example: She sculpts in clay and plaster.
items.exampleCN: 她用黏土和石膏做雕塑。

items.example: The fabric has a sculptural fold.
items.exampleCN: 这块布料有雕塑般的褶。

items.meaningCN: 雕刻成的；具雕塑造型的
items.example: The garden has sculptured hedges.
items.exampleCN: 花园里有修剪成雕塑形的树篱。

items.example: Relief sculpture covers the temple wall.
items.exampleCN: 寺庙墙面布满浮雕。

definition_zh: 雕塑的；具有雕塑感的；立体造型明显的
definition_en: relating to sculpture, or having the strong three-dimensional form associated with sculpture
core_image: 一件外套穿在模特身上，肩线像被刀削过，侧光显出清楚的块面
scene: 设计师让外套的肩部保持挺括的块面，好让它在灯下显出立体轮廓。The designer kept the jacket's shoulders crisp so that it read as sculptural under the lights.
sceneCN: 这里 sculptural 指「具有雕塑般立体感的」（第 2 个义项：形体如雕塑般明确、有块面感）；句意为设计师让外套肩线保持挺括，使它在上灯后呈现雕塑感。图中可辨识物件：外套、侧光、肩线、模特台。

derivatives.zh: 雕塑（去掉形容词后缀 -al）
在雕塑方面；以雕塑般的方式（-al 加 -ly）
雕塑家（-or 表施事者）
雕塑；造型（截短动词）

senses.title: Relating to sculpture as an art
senses.definition: connected with sculpture as a discipline, its history or its techniques
senses.definitionCN: 与作为学科的雕塑、其历史或技法相关
senses.example: The sculptural tradition of the region goes back to the sixth century.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的雕塑传统可追溯到六世纪。
senses.why: sculptural is sculpture plus the relational suffix -al, so it first means 'of sculpture'.
senses.whyCN: sculptural 是「雕塑」这一名词加表关系的后缀 -al，因此首要意思是「雕塑的」。

senses.title: Having a strong three-dimensional form
senses.definition: having a clear, modelled three-dimensional form like a sculpture
senses.definitionCN: 具有像雕塑那样明确、经过塑造的三维形体
senses.example: The dancer's pose was strikingly sculptural.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者的姿态极具雕塑感。
senses.why: viewers borrowed the adjective because a body or object can look as if it had been carved.
senses.whyCN: 观者借用了这个形容词，因为身体或物件可以看起来像被雕出来的一样。

senses.title: Of a structured clothing silhouette
senses.definition: describing clothes cut to hold a firm, shaped silhouette rather than to drape
senses.definitionCN: 描述裁剪得保持硬挺造型、而非垂坠的服装
senses.example: The collection is known for its sculptural coats.
senses.exampleCN: 这个系列以挺括有型的大衣著称。
senses.why: fashion uses the word for garments that hold their shape the way carved material does.
senses.whyCN: 时装界用这个词描述能像雕刻材料那样保持形状的衣服。

senses.title: Of form revealed by light and shadow
senses.definition: describing a photographic or cinematic look in which light defines solid form
senses.definitionCN: 描述以光线界定实体形体的摄影或电影观感
senses.example: The portrait uses hard side light for a sculptural effect.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像用硬侧光营造雕塑效果。
senses.why: photography borrowed the term because side light does to a face what a chisel does to stone.
senses.whyCN: 摄影借用这个词，因为侧光对脸做的事正如凿子对石头做的事。

senses.title: Of carving raised from a surface
senses.definition: describing relief work whose figures stand out from a flat ground
senses.definitionCN: 描述形象从平面背景凸出的浮雕作品
senses.example: A sculptural panel fills the wall above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门上方整面墙是一块浮雕板。
senses.why: relief is the branch of sculpture closest to architecture, so panels are called sculptural.
senses.whyCN: 浮雕是雕塑中最贴近建筑的分支，因此这类板件被称作雕塑式的。

senses.title: Of material suited to carving
senses.titleCN: 适合雕刻的材料质地的
senses.definition: describing a material whose mass and grain suit being carved or modelled
senses.definitionCN: 描述体量与纹理适合雕刻或塑形的材料
senses.example: The local stone is sculptural rather than brittle.
senses.exampleCN: 当地石材适合雕刻，而不易碎。
senses.why: stoneworkers call a material sculptural when it can hold a cut edge without crumbling.
senses.whyCN: 石匠把能保持切边而不崩碎的材料称作适合雕塑的。

senses.title: Of a style in art history
senses.titleCN: 艺术史中的雕塑风格的
senses.definition: describing a period style that gives weight and volume priority over colour or line
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种把体量与体积置于色彩或线条之上的时期风格
senses.example: The late paintings show a sculptural mass that earlier work lacks.
senses.exampleCN: 晚期绘画显出早期作品所缺的雕塑式体量。
senses.why: art historians use the adjective to compare painting with carving, even when no sculpture is involved.
senses.whyCN: 艺术史家用这个形容词把绘画与雕刻相比，即使画面中并无雕塑。

senses.title: Figuratively, strongly modelled in writing or music
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：文字或音乐中形体感强的
senses.definition: describing prose or music whose structure feels solidly shaped and three-dimensional
senses.definitionCN: 描述结构仿佛实体塑成、具三维感文字或音乐
senses.example: The novelist builds sculptural sentences that hold their weight.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家写出有分量的雕塑式句子。
senses.why: the abstract sense transfers the idea of firm mass from stone to structure in language and sound.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「坚实的体量」从石头转移到语言与声音的结构上。

intro.en: Sculptural is an English formation from sculpture, which comes from Latin sculptura, plus the relational suffix -al. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sculptural 是英语构词：sculpture 来自拉丁 sculptura，再加表关系的后缀 -al。年代均为约数。

items.en: The root sculpere 'to carve' is generally connected with cutting, and related forms appear in scalprum 'chisel'.
items.cn: 词根 sculpere「雕刻」一般认为与「切」相关，相关形态见于 scalprum「凿子」。

items.en: Sculptura named the act of carving and the carved object; English took the noun through French and Italian.
items.cn: sculptura 兼指雕刻动作与雕刻成品；英语经法语与意大利语借入该名词。

items.en: Sculpture settled in English in the sixteenth century, covering both the art and individual works.
items.cn: sculpture 在十六世纪定型于英语，兼指艺术与单件作品。

items.en: The Latin adjective ending -alis, through French -al, made sculptural mean 'belonging to sculpture'.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词词尾 -alis 经法语 -al 使 sculptural 表示「属于雕塑的」。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective was applied to bodies, clothes, photographs and even prose that seemed modelled.
items.cn: 自十九世纪起，这个形容词被用于仿佛经过塑形的身体、服装、照片乃至文章。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use of the adjective is not fixed to one year, and the pre-Latin base of sculpere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词最早的用例无法系于某一年，sculpere 的拉丁语前词基仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same stem that are easily swapped; group two holds adjectives describing three-dimensional or monumental form.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干、极易互换的词形；第二组是描述立体或纪念碑式形体的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the art or a work; sculptural is the adjective, so the two cannot replace each other.
entries.definitionCN: 指艺术或作品的名词；sculptural 是形容词，二者不能互换。

entries.definition: Meaning carved or shaped, often describing something actually cut, as sculptured stone.
entries.definitionCN: 意为雕刻成的，常描述真正经过切削的东西，如雕过的石头。

entries.definition: The maker of sculpture; a person noun, not a description of form.
entries.definitionCN: 雕塑的制作者；是指人名词，不描述形体。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make a three-dimensional form; it describes the act, while sculptural describes the look.
entries.definitionCN: 意为制作三维形体的动词；描述动作，而 sculptural 描述外观。

entries.definition: Describing a person, usually a tall and dignified one, who looks like a statue; it applies to people, not objects.
entries.definitionCN: 描述看起来像雕像的人，通常高挑端庄；用于人，不用于物件。

entries.definition: The plain descriptive term for having height, width and depth; it lacks the artistic suggestion of sculptural.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有高、宽、深的朴素描述词；没有 sculptural 的艺术暗示。

entries.definition: Describing something large, solid and enduring, often public; it stresses scale rather than modelled form.
entries.definitionCN: 描述巨大、坚实而持久、常为公共性的东西；强调尺度而非塑形。

entries.definition: Describing a form built up by hand, as in clay or paint; it overlaps with sculptural but stresses process.
entries.definitionCN: 描述用手堆塑成形的形体，如黏土或绘画；与 sculptural 有重合，但强调过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real design phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实设计短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sculpture + -al: the suffix turns the art noun into an adjective of relation.
normal.cn: sculpture 加 -al：后缀把艺术名词变成表关系的形容词。

normal.en: Fashion vocabulary uses it for shape that holds itself: sculptural coat, sculptural volume.
normal.cn: 时装词汇用它形容能自己撑住的形状：挺括大衣、雕塑式体积。

normal.en: Photography says sculptural lighting when hard light defines the face.
normal.cn: 摄影说雕塑式布光，指硬光把脸部形体界定出来。

normal.en: The family runs sculpture, sculptural, sculpturally, sculptor, sculpt.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sculpture、sculptural、sculpturally、sculptor、sculpt。

normal.en: Keep sculptured apart: sculptured means actually carved, sculptural means resembling sculpture.
normal.cn: 要把 sculptured 分清：前者指真的雕过，后者指像雕塑。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow sharp enough to be touched.
abstract.cn: 想象一道锐利得仿佛能摸到的影子。

abstract.en: Picture a coat standing up on its own because its shape is that firm.
abstract.cn: 想象一件大衣因为形状足够挺而自己立着。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence with weight, as if it had been cut from stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子带着分量，仿佛从石头里切出来。

examples.en: The building's sculptural staircase twists as it rises.
examples.cn: 这栋楼的雕塑式楼梯向上盘旋。

examples.en: Her photographs are admired for their sculptural light.
examples.cn: 她的照片因雕塑般的光影而受赞赏。

examples.en: The chairs have a sculptural frame in solid oak.
examples.cn: 这些椅子有实心橡木的雕塑式框架。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sculpture（雕塑）+ al（的）」——像雕塑一样的 → 具雕塑感的

root: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻」→ sculptura「雕塑」→ 英语 sculpture 加形容词后缀 -al。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses stretch from art history to fashion and photography: of sculpture, of modelled form, of structured clothes, of side light, of relief, of carvable stone, of a period style, and of shaped prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从艺术史伸向时装与摄影：雕塑的、具形体的、挺括服装的、侧光的、浮雕的、适合雕刻的石材的、时期风格的，以及有形体感的文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a form so clearly modelled that light can walk around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：形体塑得如此明确，光仿佛能绕着它走。

branches.en: ART HISTORY: the adjective marks both the discipline and a period style that prizes volume.
branches.cn: 艺术史：这个形容词既标出学科，也标出重视体量的时期风格。

branches.en: MODELLED BODY: a pose or object can look carved even when it is flesh or plastic.
branches.cn: 塑成的身体：姿态或物件即使是血肉或塑料，也能看起来像雕出来的。

branches.en: HELD SHAPE: clothing that keeps its silhouette borrows the word from carved mass.
branches.cn: 撑住的形状：能保持轮廓的服装，从雕成的体量借来这个词。

branches.en: LIGHT AND RELIEF: side light and raised carving both make form stand out from its ground.
branches.cn: 光与浮雕：侧光与凸起的雕刻都使形体从背景中凸显。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND METAPHOR: carvable stone and shaped prose both have weight that holds.
branches.cn: 材料与比喻：可雕的石材与塑成的文字都有撑得住的分量。

intro.en: Sculptural is the English adjective built on sculpture with the relational suffix -al; its parts are otherwise Latin.
intro.cn: sculptural 是英语在 sculpture 上加表关系后缀 -al 构成的形容词，其余成分来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Latin sculpere and sculptura supply the stem, while -alis 'relating to' supplies the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sculpere 与 sculptura 提供词干，-alis「与……相关」提供形容词词尾。

items.example: The root names the cutting action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名切削动作。

items.example: The noun is the base of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语词的基底。

items.meaning: the art or a work of sculpture
items.example: The museum owns one modern sculpture.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆藏有一件现代雕塑。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表关系的形容词。

items.example: The room has a sculptural ceiling.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间的天花板有雕塑感。

items.example: The two façades are sculpturally related.
items.exampleCN: 两个立面在雕塑感上相互呼应。

items.example: The sculptor approves each cast.
items.exampleCN: 雕塑家认可每一件铸件。

items.example: He sculpts with a chainsaw.
items.exampleCN: 他用链锯做雕塑。

items.example: A sculptured frieze runs above the arch.
items.exampleCN: 拱门上方有一条雕刻饰带。

definition_en: the act of cutting a shape into wood, stone or other material; an object or design made in this way
core_image: 一块木板上刻出缠绕的藤蔓，刻刀停在最后一刀，木屑卷曲落在桌面上
scene: 教堂门廊的木门上有一幅缠绕藤蔓的雕刻。The wooden door of the church porch carries a carving of winding vines.
sceneCN: 这里 carving 指「雕刻出的图案」（第 2 个义项：在木石等材料上刻出的形象或纹样）；句意为教堂门廊的木门上有一幅缠绕藤蔓的雕刻。图中可辨识物件：木门、藤蔓纹、刻刀、木屑。

derivatives.zh: 雕刻；切开（去掉名词后缀 -ing）
雕刻者；切肉者（-er 表施事者）
雕刻成的（-ed 构成形容词）
切肉刀；雕刻刀（复合名词）

senses.title: The act of cutting a shape into material
senses.definition: the process of cutting a design or figure out of wood, stone, bone or another solid material
senses.definitionCN: 从木、石、骨等固体材料中刻出图案或形象的过程
senses.example: Carving the oak panel took most of the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 刻这块橡木板花了几乎整个冬天。
senses.why: carving is the gerund of carve, so it names the cutting action before it names anything produced.
senses.whyCN: carving 是「雕刻」这一动词的动名词，因此先指切削动作，再指产生的物件。

senses.title: A carved object or design
senses.definition: an object or decorative design produced by cutting into material
senses.definitionCN: 通过刻入材料而制成的物件或装饰图案
senses.example: A carving of two birds sits above the fireplace.
senses.exampleCN: 壁炉上方有一件双鸟雕刻。
senses.why: the result sense is standard for -ing nouns: the action and its product often share one form.
senses.whyCN: 结果义在 -ing 名词中很常见：动作与其产物常共用同一形式。

senses.title: Carved decoration on furniture or architecture
senses.definition: ornamental carving applied to a surface such as a door, frame or capital
senses.definitionCN: 施加于门、框架或柱头等表面的装饰性雕刻
senses.example: The chest is decorated with carving along every edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这只箱子的每一条边都有雕饰。
senses.why: decorative carving is continuous with its surface, so the word often names the ornament rather than a separate object.
senses.whyCN: 装饰雕刻与其表面连成一体，因此这个词常指饰面纹样，而非独立物件。

senses.title: The cutting of cooked meat
senses.definition: the act of slicing a cooked joint of meat into portions for serving
senses.definitionCN: 把烤熟的整块肉切成待客小块的动作
senses.example: Carving the roast is the host's traditional job.
senses.exampleCN: 切烤肉是主人传统的活儿。
senses.why: carve has meant 'cut up food at table' since the Middle Ages, and the -ing noun kept that household sense.
senses.whyCN: 「雕刻」这一动词自中世纪起就有「在餐桌上切分食物」的意思，动名词保留了这一家庭用法。

senses.title: Wood carving as a craft
senses.definition: the craft tradition of shaping wood with chisels and knives
senses.definitionCN: 用凿子和刀具加工木材的手艺传统
senses.example: Wood carving survives in the fishing villages.
senses.exampleCN: 木雕手艺在这些渔村延续下来。
senses.why: the craft is named by its material plus the gerund, a common pattern in traditional trades.
senses.whyCN: 这门手艺以材料加动名词命名，是传统行业常见的构词方式。

senses.title: Stone or jade carving as an art
senses.definition: the art of cutting figures and ornaments from stone or jade
senses.definitionCN: 从石材或玉石中刻出形象与饰件的艺术
senses.example: Jade carving requires a patient, light hand.
senses.exampleCN: 玉雕需要耐心而轻巧的手。
senses.why: the same pattern names each material tradition, so stone carving and jade carving are separate branches.
senses.whyCN: 同一构词方式为每种材料传统命名，因此石雕与玉雕是不同分支。

senses.title: Relief work cut into a flat ground
senses.definition: carving in which the design is left standing above a recessed background
senses.definitionCN: 图案留在凹下的背景之上的雕刻方式
senses.example: The frieze shows shallow carving in soft limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 横饰带在软石灰岩上呈浅浮雕。
senses.why: relief carving cuts away the ground rather than the figure, the opposite of free-standing work.
senses.whyCN: 浮雕刻去的是背景而非形象，与独立雕刻正好相反。

senses.title: The cutting of a printing block
senses.definition: the cutting of a woodblock or similar plate to make a print
senses.definitionCN: 刻制木版或类似印版以印制图像
senses.example: Block carving demands a mirror image of the final print.
senses.exampleCN: 刻版时必须刻出与最终画面左右相反的形象。
senses.why: printing borrowed the craftsman's word because the printer cuts away what should stay white.
senses.whyCN: 印刷业借用工匠的词，因为印工要刻去那些应当留白的部分。

intro.en: Carving is the noun from the English verb carve, from Old English ceorfan 'to cut, carve'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: carving 是英语动词 carve 的名词形式，carve 来自古英语 ceorfan「切、刻」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ceorfan meant 'to cut, hew, carve', and it already covered both shaping wood and cutting up food.
items.cn: ceorfan 意为「切、砍、刻」，当时已兼指加工木材与切分食物。

items.en: The verb belongs to a Germanic family of cutting words; its Old English form is recorded, while the older common Germanic shape is reconstructed.
items.cn: 这个动词属于日耳曼语的一族「切」词；其古英语形式有据，更早的共同日耳曼语形态则属重构。

items.en: A reconstructed Indo-European root meaning 'to scratch' has been proposed, and it is also suggested as the source of Greek graphein 'to write'; this link is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 有人提出一个意为「抓划」的印欧语重构词根，并认为它也是希腊 graphein「书写」的来源；这一联系属于假说。

items.en: The -ing noun is recorded in Middle English, first for the action and soon for the thing produced.
items.cn: 带 -ing 的名词在中古英语有书证，先指动作，很快也指成品。

items.en: Carving at table and the carving knife became fixed household terms, independent of woodwork.
items.cn: 餐桌切肉与切肉刀成为固定的家庭用语，与木工无关。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the reconstructed Indo-European root and its supposed link to Greek writing words are hypotheses, not demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：所重构的印欧词根及其与希腊书写词的联系均属假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same verb and one deceptive near-homonym; group two holds cutting and shaping arts that differ from carving.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该动词的词形，外加一个易误认的近音词；第二组是区别于雕刻的切削与造型技艺。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to cut a shape or to slice meat; carving is its -ing noun.
entries.definitionCN: 意为刻出形状或切肉的动词；carving 是它的 -ing 名词。

entries.definition: A person who carves, or a carving knife and fork set; it names a person or a tool, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 雕刻者，或一套切肉刀叉；指人或工具，不指作品。

entries.definition: A strong desire, from the verb crave; it sounds close to carving but comes from a different and obscure origin.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的欲望，来自动词 crave；读音与 carving 相近，但词源不同且不甚明确。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective, meaning cut into shape, as carved oak.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，意为刻成形状的，如雕过的橡木。

entries.definition: Cutting fine lines into metal or glass, often for printing; it is incision rather than the broader shaping of carving.
entries.definitionCN: 在金属或玻璃上刻细线，常用于印刷；是刻线，而非 carving 那种整体塑形。

entries.definition: Three-dimensional art in the round; carving is the cutting method, sculpture is the finished art form.
entries.definitionCN: 独立的三维艺术；carving 是切削方法，sculpture 是完成的艺术形式。

entries.definition: Cutting small shapes from wood with a knife, typically as a pastime rather than a monument.
entries.definitionCN: 用小刀从木头上削出小物件，通常是消遣，而非纪念碑式作品。

entries.definition: Carving whose figures stand out from a flat background; it is a type of carving, defined by depth.
entries.definitionCN: 形象从平面背景凸出的雕刻；是 carving 的一种，按深度界定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real craft and household phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实手艺与家庭短语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: carve + -ing: the suffix turns the verb into an action or its product.
normal.cn: carve 加 -ing：后缀把动词变成动作或其产物。

normal.en: Material plus carving names each tradition: wood carving, stone carving, jade carving.
normal.cn: 材料加 carving 命名各传统：木雕、石雕、玉雕。

normal.en: The household pair is fixed: carving knife and carving fork.
normal.cn: 家庭成套用语固定：切肉刀与切肉叉。

normal.en: Relief carving cuts away the ground, leaving the figure standing.
normal.cn: 浮雕刻去背景，让形象留着。

normal.en: The family runs carve, carving, carver, carved.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 carve、carving、carver、carved。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf hidden in a block of wood, waiting for the knife to remove everything else.
abstract.cn: 想象木块里藏着一片叶子，等刀把其余部分都去掉。

abstract.en: Picture a negative shape left in a printing block, which becomes the white of the page.
abstract.cn: 想象印版上留下的空白形状，最终成为纸上的白。

abstract.en: Picture a family gathered while one pair of hands divides the roast.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人围坐，一双手在分切烤肉。

examples.en: The choir stalls are famous for their carving.
examples.cn: 唱诗班座椅以雕饰闻名。

examples.en: He learned carving from his grandfather.
examples.cn: 他从祖父那里学会雕刻。

examples.en: She left the carving to her brother and served the vegetables.
examples.cn: 她把切肉交给弟弟，自己去分蔬菜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「carve（刻）+ ing」——刻出来的东西 → 雕刻；雕刻品

root: 古英语 ceorfan「切、砍、刻」→ carve + -ing → carving。更早的共同日耳曼语形态及所谓印欧「抓划」词根均为重构或假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the knife: the cutting act, the carved object, ornament, the roast, woodwork, stonework, relief and the printing block.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着刀走：切削动作、刻成之物、装饰、烤肉、木工、石作、浮雕与印版。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knife taking away material until a shape is left standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀把材料一点点去掉，直到留下一个形状。

branches.en: ACT AND OBJECT: the gerund names the cutting and the thing that comes out of it.
branches.cn: 动作与物件：动名词既指切削，也指刻出的东西。

branches.en: SURFACE WORK: ornament and relief both stay attached to the material they decorate.
branches.cn: 表面作业：雕饰与浮雕都附着在所装饰的材料上。

branches.en: TABLE: the same verb cut meat long before it cut stone, and the household term survived.
branches.cn: 餐桌：同一个动词先切肉后切石，家庭用语保留了下来。

branches.en: MATERIAL TRADITIONS: wood and stone each became a named craft.
branches.cn: 材料传统：木与石各自成为有名的手艺。

branches.en: PRINT: the block is carved so that what remains prints dark.
branches.cn: 印刷：刻版时留下的部分印成深色。

intro.en: Carving is a native English verb plus the -ing suffix; the whole word is Germanic, with no Latin layer.
intro.cn: carving 是英语本族动词加 -ing 后缀；整词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁层。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin forms are listed; its near neighbour engraving is also Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，故不列拉丁词形；它的近邻 engraving 同样属日耳曼语。

items.example: The Old English verb covered both wood and meat.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词兼指木材与肉。

items.example: They carve the names into the bench.
items.exampleCN: 他们把名字刻在长凳上。

items.meaning: the act or the product of an act
items.example: The suffix makes carving a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀使 carving 成为名词。

items.example: The door carries a carving of vines.
items.exampleCN: 门上有一幅藤蔓雕刻。

items.example: The carver signs the back of the panel.
items.exampleCN: 雕刻者在板背签名。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix marks the person who cuts.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出切削的人。

items.example: Carved oak screens divide the nave.
items.exampleCN: 雕花橡木屏分隔中殿。

items.meaning: a knife for slicing cooked meat
items.example: The carving knife needs sharpening.
items.exampleCN: 切肉刀该磨了。

items.meaning: the craft of cutting wood into shapes
items.example: Wood carving uses both gouge and knife.
items.exampleCN: 木雕既用圆凿也用刀。

definition_zh: 在……上雕刻；镌刻；使深深铭记
definition_en: to cut a design or letters into a hard surface; to impress something deeply on the mind
core_image: 一枚银戒指的内圈刻着一行极细的字，放大镜下才能看清笔画
scene: 工匠用细针在金属板上刻下客户姓名的首字母。The craftsman used a fine needle to engrave the customer's initials on the metal plate.
sceneCN: 这里 engrave 指「在硬质表面刻字或刻图案」（第 1 个义项：用刀具在金属、石材等表面刻出线条）；句意为工匠用细针在金属板上刻下客户姓名的首字母。图中可辨识物件：金属板、刻针、放大镜、姓名字样。

derivatives.zh: 雕刻师；刻版师（-er 表施事者）
雕刻；版画（-ing 构成动作或结果名词）
刻有图案的（-ed 构成形容词）
镌刻物（较罕用，-ment 构成结果名词）

senses.title: To cut a design into a hard surface
senses.definition: to cut lines or a design into metal, stone, glass or another hard material
senses.definitionCN: 在金属、石材、玻璃等硬质材料上刻出线条或图案
senses.example: The machine engraves a pattern into the steel plate.
senses.exampleCN: 机器在钢板上刻出图案。
senses.why: engrave is en- 'in' plus grave 'to cut', so it literally means to cut a mark into a surface.
senses.whyCN: engrave 是 en-「进入」加 grave「切」，字面意思就是把痕迹刻进表面。

senses.title: To inscribe a name or words on an object
senses.definition: to cut letters or a short text into an object, usually as a record or gift dedication
senses.definitionCN: 把字母或短句刻在物件上，通常用于记录或赠礼题词
senses.example: They engraved her name on the trophy.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把她的名字刻在奖杯上。
senses.why: once the technique was used for words, the verb naturally took a name or a message as its object.
senses.whyCN: 当这项技术用于文字，动词便自然以姓名或词句为宾语。

senses.title: To impress something deeply on the memory
senses.definition: to fix an event or feeling in the mind so firmly that it is not forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 把事件或感受牢牢固定在心中，使其不被遗忘
senses.example: The scene was engraved on his memory for years.
senses.exampleCN: 那一幕在他记忆里刻了许多年。
senses.why: the physical cut became a metaphor for memory because both leave a mark that cannot be smoothed away.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的刻痕成为记忆的比喻，因为两者都留下无法抹平的印记。

senses.title: To prepare a printing plate by cutting
senses.definition: to cut a design into a plate so that it can be inked and printed
senses.definitionCN: 把图案刻入印版，使其能够上墨印刷
senses.example: The artist engraves the copper plate by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术家手工刻制铜版。
senses.why: printing grew out of metalwork, and the plate-maker's verb became the name of an intaglio process.
senses.whyCN: 印刷术源于金属工艺，制版者的动词后来成为凹版工艺的名称。

senses.title: To decorate glass with cut lines
senses.definition: to cut a pattern into glass for decoration, often with a wheel or acid
senses.definitionCN: 用砂轮或酸在玻璃上刻出装饰图案
senses.example: The firm engraves crystal bowls with a leaf pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在水晶碗上刻出叶片图案。
senses.why: glass cutting borrowed the word from metalwork because the action and the tool are nearly the same.
senses.whyCN: 玻璃雕刻从金属工艺借来这个词，因为动作与工具几乎相同。

senses.title: To ornament metal with cut lines
senses.definition: to decorate silver, gold or steel with cut ornamental lines
senses.definitionCN: 在银、金或钢上用刻线作装饰
senses.example: The silversmith engraves the rim with a scrolling border.
senses.exampleCN: 银匠在器口刻出卷草边饰。
senses.why: this is the oldest workshop sense, where engraving is decoration rather than writing or printing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的手工作坊义，此时镌刻是装饰，而非书写或印刷。

senses.title: To make something permanent and unforgettable
senses.titleCN: 使某事固定不变、不可磨灭
senses.definition: to establish a fact or right so firmly that it cannot be removed
senses.definitionCN: 把某项事实或权利确立得如此牢固，以致无法移除
senses.example: The ruling engraved the boundary in law.
senses.exampleCN: 该裁决把这条边界固定在法律中。
senses.why: the figurative sense extends from memory to law, where a fixed mark stands for a fixed rule.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义从记忆扩展到法律，固定的刻痕在那里代表固定的规则。

senses.title: To cut a die or mould for manufacturing
senses.definition: to cut a die, mould or roller used to stamp or shape manufactured parts
senses.definitionCN: 刻制用于冲压或成形工业零件的模具、铸型或辊筒
senses.example: Technicians engrave the roller that prints the wallpaper.
senses.exampleCN: 技师刻制印制壁纸用的辊筒。
senses.why: industrial toolmaking kept the craft verb because the die is still cut line by line.
senses.whyCN: 工业制模保留了这门手艺的动词，因为模具仍是一线一线刻出来的。

intro.en: Engrave is an English formation: the prefix en- 'in' plus grave 'to cut', from Old English grafan. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: engrave 是英语构词：前缀 en-「进入」加 grave「切」，后者来自古英语 grafan。年代均为约数。

items.en: Grafan meant 'to dig, grave, carve', and its family also produced grave 'a trench or tomb'.
items.cn: grafan 意为「挖、刻」，其词族也产生了 grave「沟、坟墓」。

items.en: The verb belongs to a Germanic family of digging and scratching words; the common Germanic shape is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 这个动词属于日耳曼语一族表示「挖、抓」的词；共同日耳曼语形态属于重构，而非有据可查。

items.en: The prefix en- 'in, into', from Latin in- through French, added the idea of cutting a mark into something.
items.cn: 前缀 en-「进入」，经法语来自拉丁 in-，增添「把痕迹刻进去」的意思。

items.en: Engrave is recorded around 1500 with the sense 'to cut into a surface', first of metal and stone.
items.cn: engrave 约在 1500 年有书证，意为「刻入表面」，最初用于金属与石材。

items.en: The printing-plate sense developed in the seventeenth century, and the memory sense followed as a metaphor.
items.cn: 印版义在十七世纪发展起来，记忆义随后作为比喻出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic base of grafan is reconstructed, and its relation to other digging roots is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：grafan 的日耳曼语前词基属于重构形式，它与其他「挖」词根的关系仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root family and one word that looks identical to the root but means something else; group two holds other ways of cutting text or images.
note.cn: 第一组是同词根词族，外加一个与词根同形却意义不同的词；第二组是刻写文字或图像的其他方式。

entries.definition: As a noun, a trench or tomb, from the same Old English family as grafan 'dig'; as an adjective it means serious, from a different source.
entries.definitionCN: 作名词指沟或坟墓，与古英语 grafan「挖」同族；作形容词意为严肃，来源不同。

entries.definition: A person who cuts designs into metal, stone or glass; the agent noun names the worker, not the action.
entries.definitionCN: 在金属、石材或玻璃上刻图案的人；施事名词指工人，不指动作。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective, meaning decorated or marked by cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，意为刻有图案或记号的。

entries.definition: The -ing noun for the process or for a print taken from an engraved plate.
entries.definitionCN: 带 -ing 的名词，指过程或从刻版印出的图画。

entries.definition: To cut a shape out of wood or stone; it removes material to create form, while engrave cuts lines into a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 从木石中刻出形状；通过去除材料造形，而 engrave 是在表面刻线。

entries.definition: To write or cut words on a surface, especially as a dedication; it stresses the text rather than the technique.
entries.definitionCN: 在表面书写或刻写文字，尤指题献；强调文字内容而非技法。

entries.definition: To cut a design with acid rather than a tool, a different technique with a similar printed result.
entries.definitionCN: 用酸而非刀具蚀刻图案，技术不同但印刷效果相近。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to cut lines into a surface, often used in archaeology and surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 正式动词，意为在表面刻线，常用于考古与外科。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real workshop phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实作坊短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: en- 'in' + grave 'cut': to cut a mark into the surface.
normal.cn: en-「进入」+ grave「切」：把痕迹刻进表面。

normal.en: The same Old English root gives grave, the dug trench, and engrave, the cut mark.
normal.cn: 同一古英语词根给出 grave「挖出的沟」与 engrave「刻出的痕」。

normal.en: Workshop phrases show the craft: engrave a name, engrave a plate, engraved glass.
normal.cn: 作坊短语显示手艺：刻名字、刻印版、刻花玻璃。

normal.en: The metaphor is fixed: engraved on the memory, engraved in the heart.
normal.cn: 比喻已固定：铭刻在记忆中、铭刻在心上。

normal.en: The family runs engrave, engraver, engraving, engraved.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 engrave、engraver、engraving、engraved。

abstract.en: Picture a mark so thin that only a magnifying glass proves it is there.
abstract.cn: 想象一道细痕，只有放大镜才能证明它存在。

abstract.en: Picture a memory with a groove worn into it, deeper each time it is recalled.
abstract.cn: 想象一段记忆被磨出一道沟，每次回想都更深。

abstract.en: Picture a steel roller that carries an entire wallpaper pattern in shallow lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一根钢辊，用浅浅的线条承载整幅壁纸图案。

examples.en: The ring was engraved with her initials.
examples.cn: 戒指上刻有她姓名的首字母。

examples.en: They engrave the glass with a diamond wheel.
examples.cn: 他们用金刚石轮在玻璃上刻花。

examples.en: The date is engraved on the memorial stone.
examples.cn: 日期刻在纪念石上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en（进入）+ grave（刻/墓）」——把字刻进石头 → 雕刻、镌刻

root: 古英语 grafan「挖、刻」→ grave「切」；加前缀 en-「进入」构成 engrave。更早的日耳曼语前词基为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one cut line: into steel, into a trophy, into memory, into a printing plate, into glass, into silver, into law, and into a manufacturing die.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一条刻线展开：刻入钢、刻入奖杯、刻入记忆、刻入印版、刻入玻璃、刻入银器、刻入法律，最后刻入工业模具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp point opening a thin line that cannot be smoothed away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个尖点划开一道细线，再也抹不平。

branches.en: CUTTING SURFACES: metal and glass are marked by the same opening of a line.
branches.cn: 刻入表面：金属与玻璃都靠划开线条留下记号。

branches.en: WRITING AND ORNAMENT: letters on a trophy and scrollwork on silver are both cut decoration.
branches.cn: 文字与装饰：奖杯上的字母与银器上的卷草，都是刻出的装饰。

branches.en: PRINTING AND TOOLS: the plate and the die are cut so that they can reproduce a mark.
branches.cn: 印刷与工具：印版与模具被刻出来，是为了复制记号。

branches.en: MEMORY: a cut in metal stands for a mark that experience leaves in the mind.
branches.cn: 记忆：金属上的刻痕，比喻经验在心上留下的印。

branches.en: PERMANENCE: law borrows the image to say that a rule cannot be removed.
branches.cn: 永久：法律借这个意象表示规则不可移除。

intro.en: Engrave is a Germanic root with a Latin-derived prefix: en- 'in' plus grave 'cut'. The combination is English, not Latin.
intro.cn: engrave 是日耳曼词根加拉丁来源前缀：en-「进入」加 grave「切」，但组合本身是英语构词，并非拉丁词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix en- came into English through French from Latin in-, but the root grave is Germanic, so the word has no Latin ancestor of its own.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 en- 经法语从拉丁 in- 进入英语，但词根 grave 属日耳曼语，因此这个词本身没有拉丁语祖先。

items.example: The Old English verb also gave grave, a dug trench.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词也产生了 grave「挖出的沟」。

items.example: The verb survives mainly inside engrave.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词主要保存在 engrave 中。

items.structure: en- (prefix, 'in, into', from Latin in- via French)
items.example: The prefix puts the cut inside the surface.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把切削放进表面之内。

items.example: They engrave the plate before inking it.
items.exampleCN: 他们先刻版，再上墨。

items.example: The suffix makes engraver from engrave.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 engrave 变成 engraver。

items.example: The engraver works under a lens.
items.exampleCN: 雕刻师在放大镜下工作。

items.example: The suffix supplies the noun engraving.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀提供名词 engraving。

items.example: An engraved date marks the rim.
items.exampleCN: 器口刻着一个日期。

items.meaning: an invitation printed from an engraved plate
items.example: The wedding used engraved invitations.
items.exampleCN: 婚礼使用了刻版请柬。

definition_en: the art or process of cutting a design into a hard surface; a print made from an engraved plate
core_image: 一张压在纸上的铜版画，墨线细密，边缘留着版压出的凹痕
scene: 修复师把一张旧版画从纸夹里取出，对着光看纸上的压痕。The restorer lifted an old engraving from its folder and held it to the light.
sceneCN: 这里 engraving 指「版画」（第 2 个义项：从刻版上印出的图画）；句意为修复师从纸夹中取出一张旧版画，对着光查看压痕。图中可辨识物件：版画纸、压痕、纸夹、台灯。

derivatives.zh: 雕刻；镌刻（去掉 -ing）
雕刻师；刻版师（-er 表施事者）
刻有图案的（-ed 构成形容词）
镌刻物（较罕用）

senses.title: The art or process of cutting a design
senses.definition: the craft of cutting lines or a design into metal, stone or glass
senses.definitionCN: 在金属、石材或玻璃上刻出线条或图案的技艺
senses.example: Engraving requires a steady hand and a good lens.
senses.exampleCN: 雕刻需要稳健的手和好的放大镜。
senses.why: engraving is the gerund of engrave, so it names the process before it names any print.
senses.whyCN: engraving 是「雕刻」这一动词的动名词，因此先指过程，再指印件。

senses.title: A print taken from an engraved plate
senses.definition: a picture printed from a plate whose lines were cut by hand
senses.definitionCN: 从手工刻线的印版上印出的图画
senses.example: The book contains twenty engravings of the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书里有二十幅海岸版画。
senses.why: printers named the printed sheet by the process that made the plate, a common trade shorthand.
senses.whyCN: 印刷者用制版工艺来命名印成的纸页，这是行业里常见的简称。

senses.title: The engraved plate or block itself
senses.definition: the metal plate or block carrying the cut design from which prints are made
senses.definitionCN: 载有刻出图案、用于印制的金属版或版块
senses.example: The original engraving survives in the museum store.
senses.exampleCN: 原刻版保存在博物馆库房。
senses.why: the same noun covers the tool and its product because the plate is the meeting point of both.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词兼指工具与产物，因为印版正是两者的交汇处。

senses.title: Engraved lettering or ornament on an object
senses.definition: letters or ornament cut into a metal, glass or stone object
senses.definitionCN: 刻在金属、玻璃或石质物件上的文字或装饰
senses.example: The cup's engraving names the winning crew.
senses.exampleCN: 杯子上的刻字写着获胜船队的名字。
senses.why: the gerund also names the resulting marks when the marks are the notable feature of the object.
senses.whyCN: 当刻出的痕迹成为物件显著特征时，动名词也指这些痕迹。

senses.title: Wood engraving as a relief method
senses.definition: a relief printing method using a block cut across the grain with fine tools
senses.definitionCN: 用细工具在横切木块上刻制的凸版印刷方法
senses.example: Wood engraving allowed finer lines than the older woodcut.
senses.exampleCN: 木口木刻能刻出比旧式木刻更细的线。
senses.why: the material and method are named together, distinguishing this branch from metal engraving.
senses.whyCN: 材料与方法一起命名，从而与金属雕刻区分开来。

senses.title: Intaglio engraving on copper or steel
senses.definition: the intaglio method in which lines are cut below the plate surface and hold the ink
senses.definitionCN: 把线条刻到版面以下、使线条含墨的凹版方法
senses.example: Copper engraving reproduces tone with astonishing fineness.
senses.exampleCN: 铜版雕刻能以惊人的精细度再现色调。
senses.why: the cut line sits below the surface, so the plate prints what the burin removed rather than what it left.
senses.whyCN: 刻线低于版面，因此印出的是刻刀去掉的部分，而非留下的部分。

senses.title: Decorative engraving on silverware
senses.definition: ornamental cutting applied to silver, gold or plate for decoration
senses.definitionCN: 为装饰而在银、金或器皿上进行的刻饰
senses.example: The teapot's engraving shows a family crest.
senses.exampleCN: 茶壶上的刻饰是一枚家族纹章。
senses.why: before printing existed, engraving was chiefly this workshop decoration, and the sense remains.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷术出现之前，镌刻主要是这种作坊装饰，这一义项延续至今。

senses.title: Security engraving on banknotes
senses.definition: the fine engraved lines used in security printing to make copying difficult
senses.definitionCN: 安全印刷中用于增加复制难度的精细刻线
senses.example: Banknote engraving uses lines too fine for most scanners.
senses.exampleCN: 钞票雕刻使用的线条细到多数扫描仪难以还原。
senses.why: security printing inherited intaglio engraving because cut lines can hold special inks and resist reproduction.
senses.whyCN: 安全印刷继承凹版雕刻，因为刻线能承载特殊油墨并难以复制。

intro.en: Engraving is engrave plus the English suffix -ing; engrave itself is en- 'in' plus grave 'cut', from Old English grafan. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: engraving 是 engrave 加英语后缀 -ing；engrave 本身是 en-「进入」加 grave「切」，后者来自古英语 grafan。年代均为约数。

items.en: Grafan meant 'to dig, carve', and the same family produced grave, a dug trench or tomb.
items.cn: grafan 意为「挖、刻」，同一词族也产生 grave「挖出的沟或坟」。

items.en: Engrave is recorded around 1500 meaning 'to cut into a surface', first in metalwork.
items.cn: engrave 约在 1500 年有书证，意为「刻入表面」，最初用于金属工艺。

items.en: In the seventeenth century engraving came to name both the cut plate and the print taken from it.
items.cn: 十七世纪，engraving 兼指刻成的版与从版上印出的画。

items.en: Copper and steel intaglio, wood engraving and later security printing each kept the same noun.
items.cn: 铜钢凹版、木口木刻以及后来的安全印刷都沿用同一个名词。

items.en: Print collecting made the countable plural engravings standard for individual prints.
items.cn: 版画收藏使可数复数 engravings 成为单幅印件的标准说法。
