items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic base of grafan is reconstructed, so any older root proposed for it remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：grafan 的日耳曼语前词基属于重构形式，为它提出的更早词根仍属假说。

note.en: Group one holds the engrave family and a French-derived look-alike; group two holds other printmaking and carving terms.
note.cn: 第一组是 engrave 词族，外加一个法语来源的形近词；第二组是其他版画与雕刻术语。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to cut into a surface; engraving is its process noun and also the print.
entries.definitionCN: 意为刻入表面的动词；engraving 是其过程名词，也指印件。

entries.definition: The worker who cuts the plate or the ornament; it names a person, not a print.
entries.definitionCN: 刻制印版或刻饰的工人；指人，不指印件。

entries.definition: A French-derived term for photogravure or rotogravure printing; it shares the concept but not the English word's formation.
entries.definitionCN: 来自法语，指照相凹版或轮转凹版印刷；概念相通，但并非同一个英语构词。

entries.definition: The past participle describing an object that has been cut or decorated, as engraved glass.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，描述已被刻过或刻饰的物件，如刻花玻璃。

entries.definition: A print made by biting lines with acid rather than cutting them; the lines are freer and less mechanical.
entries.definitionCN: 用酸腐蚀线条而非刻线的版画；线条更自由，少了机械感。

entries.definition: A print from a plank cut along the grain, with the design left standing; older and coarser than wood engraving.
entries.definitionCN: 沿木纹纵切、留下凸起图案的木版印件；比木口木刻更古老粗犷。

entries.definition: Any picture pressed from a prepared surface onto paper; engraving is one kind of print.
entries.definitionCN: 从制好的版面压印到纸上的任何图画；engraving 是其中一种。

entries.definition: Cutting a three-dimensional shape out of wood or stone; engraving cuts lines rather than whole forms.
entries.definitionCN: 从木石中刻出三维形状；engraving 刻的是线，而非整体造型。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real printmaking terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实版画术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: engrave + -ing: the suffix gives both the process and the printed sheet.
normal.cn: engrave 加 -ing：后缀既给出过程，也给出印成的纸页。

normal.en: Methods are named by material: copper engraving, steel engraving, wood engraving.
normal.cn: 方法按材料命名：铜版、钢版、木口木刻。

normal.en: A print collection speaks of engravings, plural, for individual sheets.
normal.cn: 版画收藏用复数 engravings 指单幅印件。

normal.en: Intaglio means the line sits below the plate and holds the ink.
normal.cn: 凹版意味着线条低于版面并含住油墨。

normal.en: The family runs engrave, engraver, engraving, engraved.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 engrave、engraver、engraving、engraved。

abstract.en: Picture a line cut below the surface, carrying ink the way a ditch carries water.
abstract.cn: 想象一条刻在表面以下的线，像沟渠蓄水一样含着墨。

abstract.en: Picture a metal plate that outlives every sheet printed from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块金属版，比从它印出的每一张纸都活得久。

abstract.en: Picture a banknote whose fine lines cannot be photographed cleanly.
abstract.cn: 想象一张钞票，其细线无法被干净地拍下来。

examples.en: The gallery owns engravings by three centuries of artists.
examples.cn: 画廊藏有三个世纪以来艺术家的版画。

examples.en: Copper engraving was the standard illustration method in the eighteenth century.
examples.cn: 铜版画是十八世纪的标准插图方法。

examples.en: The trophy's engraving had worn almost smooth.
examples.cn: 奖杯上的刻字几乎磨平了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「engrave（刻）+ ing」——刻出来的画 → 版画；雕刻

root: 古英语 grafan「挖、刻」→ engrave 加 -ing → engraving；既是雕刻过程，也是刻版与版画。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the cutting act to the printed sheet, the plate, the lettering, wood blocks, copper plates, silver ornament and banknotes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从切削动作走向印成的纸页、印版、刻字、木版、铜版、银器饰刻与钞票。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut line holding ink, pressed onto paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条含住油墨的刻线，被压到纸上。

branches.en: PROCESS AND TOOL: the cutting and the plate are two stages of one craft.
branches.cn: 过程与工具：刻制与印版是同一门手艺的两个阶段。

branches.en: PRINT: the sheet is named after the method that made its plate.
branches.cn: 印件：纸页以制版方法命名。

branches.en: ORNAMENT: lettering on a cup and scrollwork on silver stay with the object.
branches.cn: 装饰：杯上的刻字与银器上的卷草都留在物件上。

branches.en: METHODS: wood block and copper plate split the craft by material and depth.
branches.cn: 方法：木版与铜版按材料与深度把工艺分开。

branches.en: SECURITY: the finest lines move from art to banknote protection.
branches.cn: 防伪：最精细的线条从艺术走向钞票保护。

intro.en: Engraving adds the English -ing suffix to engrave, itself a Germanic root with a Latin-derived prefix.
intro.cn: engraving 在 engrave 上加英语 -ing 后缀，而 engrave 本身是日耳曼词根加拉丁来源前缀。

latinIntro.en: The prefix en- passes through French from Latin in-, but the root is Germanic, so no Latin root forms are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 en- 经法语来自拉丁 in-，但词根属日耳曼语，故此处不列拉丁词根形式。

items.example: The root underlies both grave and engrave.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时支撑 grave 与 engrave。

items.example: They engrave the plate with a burin.
items.exampleCN: 他们用刻刀在版上刻线。

items.meaning: the act, or the thing produced
items.example: The suffix makes the process a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把过程变成名词。

items.example: The engraving hangs above the desk.
items.exampleCN: 那幅版画挂在书桌上方。

items.example: The engraver cut the lettering by hand.
items.exampleCN: 雕刻师手工刻出文字。

items.example: An engraved bowl stood on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 架子上有一只刻花碗。

items.meaning: intaglio printing from a copper plate
items.example: Copper engraving reproduces fine detail.
items.exampleCN: 铜版画能再现精细细节。

items.meaning: relief printing from an end-grain block
items.example: Wood engraving uses a boxwood block.
items.exampleCN: 木口木刻使用黄杨木块。

items.meaning: the plate that carries the cut design
items.example: The engraving plate is stored in acid-free paper.
items.exampleCN: 刻版存放在无酸纸中。

definition_en: words cut or written on a hard surface, such as stone or metal; the act of writing them
core_image: 一块风化的石碑，凹下去的字口里积着灰，侧光把每一笔照出阴影
scene: 游客在石碑前停下，辨认那行被风磨浅的刻字。Visitors stopped before the stone to read the weathered inscription.
sceneCN: 这里 inscription 指「刻在石头上的铭文」（第 1 个义项：刻写在坚硬表面上的文字）；句意为游客在石碑前停下来辨认那段被风磨蚀的铭文。图中可辨识物件：石碑、字口、侧光、围栏。

derivatives.zh: 题写；刻写（去掉名词后缀 -ion）
铭文的；铭刻的（-al 构成形容词）
刻有文字的（-ed 构成形容词）
以铭刻方式（较罕用）

senses.title: Words cut or written on a hard surface
senses.titleCN: 刻写在硬质表面上的文字
senses.definition: a short text cut, carved or written on stone, metal or another durable surface
senses.definitionCN: 刻、凿或写在石、金属等耐久表面上的短篇文字
senses.example: The inscription on the lintel names the builder.
senses.exampleCN: 门楣上的铭文写着建造者的名字。
senses.why: inscription comes from Latin inscribere 'to write in', so it names what has been written onto a surface.
senses.whyCN: inscription 来自拉丁 inscribere「写入」，因此指被写到表面上的文字。

senses.title: The act of writing or cutting such words
senses.definition: the act of writing, cutting or dedicating words on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面书写、刻写或题献文字的行为
senses.example: The inscription of the names took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 刻写这些名字花了三天。
senses.why: the Latin noun of action named the writing before it named the written text, and both senses survive.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁行为名词先指书写动作，后指写成的文字，两义都保留下来。

senses.title: A dedication written in a book
senses.definition: a short handwritten dedication on the title page or flyleaf of a book
senses.definitionCN: 写在书名页或扉页上的简短手书题献
senses.example: The flyleaf carries an inscription from the author.
senses.exampleCN: 扉页上有作者亲笔题词。
senses.why: books extended the word from stone to paper because a dedication is still words written into an object.
senses.whyCN: 书籍把这个词从石头扩展到纸张，因为题献仍是写进物件里的文字。

senses.title: An inscribed text studied as evidence
senses.definition: a written text on a durable object studied by historians and archaeologists
senses.definitionCN: 写在耐久物件上、被历史学家与考古学家研究的文字
senses.example: The inscription dates the bridge to the reign of that emperor.
senses.exampleCN: 铭文把这座桥定在该皇帝在位时期。
senses.why: epigraphy treats inscriptions as documents, because a cut text outlasts the paper record.
senses.whyCN: 铭文学把铭文当作文献，因为刻写的文字比纸质记录更耐久。

senses.title: The legend on a coin or medal
senses.definition: the lettering and titles struck around the edge or field of a coin or medal
senses.definitionCN: 铸在钱币或奖章边缘或版面上的文字与称号
senses.example: The coin's inscription includes the mint mark.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚钱币的铭文包含造币厂标记。
senses.why: numismatics borrowed the word for struck lettering, which serves the same record-keeping purpose.
senses.whyCN: 钱币学借这个词指铸出的文字，其作用同样是记录。

senses.title: The text on a gravestone
senses.definition: the epitaph or identifying text cut into a gravestone
senses.definitionCN: 刻在墓碑上的墓志或身份文字
senses.example: The inscription gives only a name and two dates.
senses.exampleCN: 碑文只留下一个名字和两个日期。
senses.why: gravestones are the commonest place most people meet the word, and the sense became fixed there.
senses.whyCN: 墓碑是大多数人遇见这个词的最常见场合，该义项在此固定下来。

senses.title: Dedication text on an award or trophy
senses.definition: the dedicatory words engraved on a cup, plate or medal given as a prize
senses.definitionCN: 刻在作为奖品颁发的杯、盘或奖章上的题献文字
senses.example: The trophy's inscription misspells the team's name.
senses.exampleCN: 奖杯上的题刻把队名拼错了。
senses.why: award practice borrowed the word because the cup records the win in permanent lettering.
senses.whyCN: 颁奖惯例借用这个词，因为奖杯用永久文字记录胜利。

senses.title: Formal recording in a public register
senses.titleCN: 在公共登记簿中的正式登记（法律义）
senses.definition: the formal entry of a right, charge or fact in a public register, as in civil-law systems
senses.definitionCN: 在大陆法系中把权利、负担或事实正式登入公共登记簿
senses.example: The mortgage requires inscription in the land register.
senses.exampleCN: 该抵押须在土地登记簿中登记。
senses.why: civil law uses the word for writing a right into the public record, keeping the literal sense of writing in.
senses.whyCN: 大陆法用这个词表示把权利写入公共记录，保留了「写入」的字面义。

intro.en: Inscription comes from Latin inscriptio, from inscribere 'to write in or on', built on in- 'in' and scribere 'to write'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inscription 来自拉丁 inscriptio，源自动词 inscribere「写入、写在上面」，由 in-「在内」与 scribere「书写」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Scribere meant 'to write'. It is generally connected with an idea of scratching or cutting a mark, and the reconstructed Indo-European base often cited for it is not directly attested.
items.cn: scribere 意为「书写」。一般认为它与「抓划、刻痕」的概念相关，常为其引用的印欧语重构词基并非直接有据。

items.en: In- 'in, on' plus scribere made inscribere 'to write in or on something, to enrol'.
items.cn: in-「在内、在上」加 scribere 构成 inscribere「写入、写在上面、登记」。

items.en: The noun inscriptio named the act of writing in and the text so written, a double sense English kept.
items.cn: 名词 inscriptio 兼指写入动作与写成的文字，英语保留了这个双重含义。

items.en: English took inscription through French in the sixteenth century, first for texts on stone and metal.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪经法语借入 inscription，最初指石与金属上的文字。

items.en: Scholarship made inscriptions a source for dating, while civil law kept a technical sense of registration.
items.cn: 学术研究把铭文当作断代依据，大陆法则保留了「登记」这一专门义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin base of scribere is reconstructed, and its exact relation to other cutting roots is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：scribere 的拉丁语前词基属于重构形式，它与其他「切」词根的确切关系仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin verb and a look-alike built with a different prefix; group two holds words for short texts on objects or graves.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词的词形，外加一个用不同前缀构成的形近词；第二组是刻在物件或墓碑上的短篇文字。

entries.definition: To write or cut words on a surface; inscription is its action noun and its result.
entries.definitionCN: 在表面书写或刻写文字；inscription 是其行为名词与结果。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of inscriptions', used of lettering styles and evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「铭文的」形容词，用于字体风格与证据。

entries.definition: Sub- 'under' plus scriptio: a payment or a signed agreement, not a text cut on stone.
entries.definitionCN: sub-「在下」加 scriptio：指付款或签署协议，不是刻在石头上的文字。

entries.definition: The past participle describing an object that bears written or cut words.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，描述载有书写或刻写文字的物件。

entries.definition: A text placed at the head of a book or cut on a building; it is a kind of inscription, often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 置于书首或刻在建筑上的文字；是铭文的一种，常偏文学性。

entries.definition: The words on a tomb, specifically commemorating the dead; narrower than inscription.
entries.definitionCN: 墓上的文字，专为纪念死者；比 inscription 范围更窄。

entries.definition: The lettering on a coin or the explanatory text on a map; it is one specialised kind of inscription.
entries.definitionCN: 钱币上的文字或地图的说明文字；是铭文的一种专门类型。

entries.definition: Words offering a book, building or work to someone; an inscription may carry a dedication.
entries.definitionCN: 把书、建筑或作品献给某人的话；铭文可以承载题献。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real epigraphic terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实铭文学术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'in' + scribere 'write' + -ion: the writing in, and what is written in.
normal.cn: in-「在内」+ scribere「写」+ -ion：写进去的动作，以及写进去的字。

normal.en: The family runs inscribe, inscription, inscriptional, inscribed.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 inscribe、inscription、inscriptional、inscribed。

normal.en: The same scribere root gives describe, prescribe, subscribe and script.
normal.cn: 同一 scribere 词根给出 describe、prescribe、subscribe 与 script。

normal.en: Epigraphy is the study of inscriptions; the word names both the text and the discipline.
normal.cn: 铭文学是研究铭文的学问；这个词兼指文字与学科。

normal.en: Coins and trophies carry inscriptions too, not only stone monuments.
normal.cn: 钱币与奖杯也带铭文，并不只有石碑。

abstract.en: Picture letters sunk below the surface of stone, holding shadow instead of ink.
abstract.cn: 想象字母凹在石头表面之下，盛着阴影而不是墨。

abstract.en: Picture a name that outlasts everyone who could have spoken it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字比所有可能说出它的人都活得久。

abstract.en: Picture a flyleaf with three handwritten words that turn a book into a gift.
abstract.cn: 想象扉页上三个手写的字，把一本书变成一份礼物。

examples.en: The inscription was too worn to read without a lamp.
examples.cn: 铭文磨损得太厉害，不打灯就读不出来。

examples.en: He found a Latin inscription beneath the plaster.
examples.cn: 他在灰泥下面发现了一段拉丁文铭文。

examples.en: The author's inscription made the book valuable.
examples.cn: 作者的题词使这本书变得珍贵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（里面）+ script（写）+ ion」——写进石头里的字 → 铭文

root: 拉丁 in-「在内」+ scribere「书写」→ inscribere「写入」→ inscriptio「铭文；题写」。scribere 的拉丁语前词基为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of writing in: on stone, in the act itself, in a book, in the historical record, on a coin, on a grave, on a trophy, and in a public register.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「写入」这一动作展开：写进石头、写这一动作本身、写进书页、写进史料、写进钱币、写进墓碑、写进奖杯，最后写进公共登记簿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters pressed into a surface so that the material itself becomes the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：字母被压进表面，材料本身成了书页。

branches.en: TEXT AND ACT: the cut words and the cutting of them share one noun.
branches.cn: 文字与动作：刻出的字与刻这个动作共用一个名词。

branches.en: OFFERED WORDS: a book flyleaf and a trophy both carry words given to someone.
branches.cn: 献出的字：书籍扉页与奖杯都承载献给某人的话。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: stone texts and coin legends are read as dated records.
branches.cn: 证据：石刻文字与钱币铭文都被读作有年代的记录。

branches.en: GRAVE: the commonest meeting point of the word is a name cut in stone.
branches.cn: 墓碑：这个词最常见的相遇之处，是刻在石头上的名字。

branches.en: LAW: civil-law registration turns writing into a legal fact.
branches.cn: 法律：大陆法登记把书写变成一项法律事实。

intro.en: Inscription is built from Latin in- 'in', scribere 'write' and the noun ending -tio; English also uses the verb inscribe and the adjective inscriptional.
intro.cn: inscription 由拉丁 in-「在内」、scribere「书写」与名词词尾 -tio 构成；英语另有动词 inscribe 与形容词 inscriptional。

latinIntro.en: Latin scribere gives inscribe, describe, prescribe, subscribe and script; in- adds 'in or on', and -tio forms the action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 scribere 衍生 inscribe、describe、prescribe、subscribe 与 script；in- 增添「在内、在上」，-tio 构成行为名词。

items.example: The prefix places the writing on a surface.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把书写置于表面之上。

items.structure: scribere, scripsi, scriptum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root supplies the act of writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供书写动作。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of inscription.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 inscription 的直接来源。

items.example: The ending forms the noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成行为名词。

items.meaning: writing in; a text on a surface
items.example: The inscription faces the road.
items.exampleCN: 铭文朝向大路。

items.meaning: to write or cut words on
items.example: They inscribe the date inside the ring.
items.exampleCN: 他们把日期刻在戒指内侧。

items.example: Inscriptional evidence supports the early date.
items.exampleCN: 铭文证据支持这一较早的年代。

items.example: An inscribed stone marks the well.
items.exampleCN: 一块刻字的石头标出井的位置。

items.example: The prefix sub- changes the meaning entirely.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 彻底改变了词义。
